acceptance_criteria: Exegra's format has contract exposure and structured auth; free-text auth is refused when system.generation is on; docs and tests

Validation rules, each with a test: a public state-changing contract requires a session with CSRF and origin, or a verified signature; anonymous is allowed only on public contracts marked read-only or explicitly justified, and each such contract has a quota; internal and local contracts are never routable through the gateway; every contract naming a policy references a policy that exists; a service credential is never accepted on a public route
Strata's spec states exposure and auth for all 291 contracts, mapped from the prose and checked against what the running services do; contracts whose prose is ambiguous are listed for review

specc generates the authorizer from the schemes (no string matching), default deny for anything unstated, and the gateway's route table only for public contracts; tests show an internal contract is unreachable through the gateway and each scheme refuses a missing or wrong credential
Gate and Playwright pass
tasks.description: Asked 2026-11-19 (security posture). Every contract's auth is free prose: 37 distinct sentences over 291 contracts (e.g. 'Anyone; no session is needed' x38, 'A principal whose policies permit the operation' x40, 'Local call inside the platform process' x92). specc copies the sentence into ContractSpec.auth and the runtime hands it to a hand-written Authorizer; the only Authorizer (ServiceToken, crates/runtime/src/routes.rs:206-230) lets 'none' through and demands the service token for every other string, so meaning lives in string matching. The spec has 0 policies, so 'policies permit' is unenforced in generated code. There is no public/private split. Make auth checkable data: each contract states its exposure (public: reachable from browsers/internet through the gateway; internal: service network only; local: in-process) and a structured auth (scheme: anonymous, session, service credential, provisioning token, signature of a named secret, signed address, delegation; plus required roles or policy ids, CSRF and origin for browser sessions, step-up where needed). Validation makes the posture airtight by construction.
tasks.title: Auth as structured spec: public vs private exposure, schemes, default deny, generated authorizer

tasks.description:
Asked 2026-11-19: for every issue found by the reviews (WG-4887, WG-4888, WG-4909, WG-4886, WG-4895), specc must refuse with an error when run on a spec that lacks the thing found. Rules live in Exegra (validate with system.generation on) or in specc (target-specific refusals); specc must refuse to generate at all unless the spec's Exegra validation under generation is clean. Each rule gets a negative fixture: a minimal spec missing exactly that thing, and a test that specc refuses it with the named code.

Mapping (finding -> rule -> task that adds it):
1 prose contract auth -> contract.auth-structured (WG-4908)
2 contract without exposure public/internal/local -> contract.exposure (WG-4908)
3 public state-changing contract without session+CSRF+origin or signature -> auth.public-write (WG-4908)
4 anonymous contract without read-only flag or quota -> auth.anonymous (WG-4908)
5 contract naming an undefined policy -> auth.policy-unknown (WG-4908)
6 development/fixture contracts reachable outside development, or tenant-exposed contracts returning other tenants' or platform data -> auth.dev-only, contract.tenant-scope (WG-4908, WG-4918)
7 domain event without a telemetry statement; a logged field of a sensitive type -> telemetry.* (WG-4896)
8 uiScenario steps the e2e generator cannot generate; check-e2e not run -> specc e2e refuses and the gate runs check-e2e (WG-4897)
9 identifiers that collide, are reserved or start with digits; comment/literal text that cannot be emitted safely -> specc diagnostics (WG-4898)
10 routes of equal specificity -> route.ambiguous (WG-4900)
11 validation/record patterns whose meaning differs between Rust and JS; unanchored record patterns -> validation.pattern-portable (WG-4900)
12 machine storage key not the record's whole key; machine state not tenant-scoped -> storage.key-whole, storage.tenant-scope (WG-4907)
13 time compared with a literal baseline; unguarded time differences; delays not representable in ms; integer literals beyond the shared bound -> time.epoch, time.difference, delay.unit, number.bound (WG-4902)
14 elapsed (timer-only) events reachable as external inputs -> event.elapsed-external (WG-4905)
15 idempotent contracts without a replay scope -> contract.idempotency-scope (WG-4906)
16 computed timer delays without one rule; browser jitter not modelled; stale traces or generated files -> timer.computed, machine.jitter, trace.stale (WG-4904)
17 scenario faults the runtime cannot produce; machines whose initial state the Host cannot reproduce -> fault.unrealisable, machine.initial-unreachable (WG-4903)
18 implementation machine on a not-implemented component not marked target; model scaffolding fields in shipped records -> behavior.realisation-subject, record.scaffolding (WG-4922, WG-4924)
19 requirement realised by construction whose realising code is target-only or not linked into a shipped binary -> requirement.construction-unshipped (WG-4921, WG-4923)
20 contract error variants without status; error bodies exposing internal fields -> contract.error-status, contract.error-body (WG-4893)
21 deployable component without start information in the spec (ports, env, health, volumes) -> deploy.component-start, replacing specifications/deploy.jsonc (WG-4892 follow-up)
22 emitted events with no receiver in the generated dispatcher's routing -> emit.unrouted (WG-4901)

tasks.description: Raised 2026-11-19. The running store is a metadata model (storage-sqlite: tenants with schema JSON, schema_history, generic records(tenant, object, id, version, data JSON), record_index, events, journal, snapshots, sessions, accounts); object types, fields, constraints, workflows and policies are tenant data (tenants/_templates/publication.json). The spec does not say so: its records section declares tenant content as fixed record types (rec-content with CDN fields and a fields map), specc generates fixed structs for them, and the kernel's own types are stand-ins (intent {kind,payload}, schema as string). Nothing separates platform records (tenants, schema versions, sessions, accounts, events, journal, snapshots: fixed tables) from tenant domain data (described only by a tenant schema, as data). Also: TEN-001 requires a database per tenant; today all tenants share one SQLite file separated by a tenant column, and the Postgres adapter and control plane are not implemented.

Profiles (avatars), badges (artwork) and content management all need files held per tenant (k-2).
tasks.title: File store with upload scanning and signed media addresses

acceptance_criteria: A published record is found by a search of its tenant after its commit, and an unpublished one is not found by a visitor (SRH-150).
A search in one tenant returns no record of another tenant.
Deleting or unpublishing a record removes it from results.
The index is rebuilt from the tenant's records alone and yields the same results.
tasks.description: Component search-index is "not-implemented". Contracts index-record and search exist, with SRH-150 (a search returns only the published records the reader's audience class permits) and ng-10 (no search across tenants). Needed for content management and for finding people and profiles.
tasks.title: Search index per tenant

acceptance_criteria: A tenant at its plan's request rate is refused at the gateway with the quota's declared error while another tenant on the same process is served.
A write past the plan's stored-records or stored-bytes limit is refused (write-quota-flow), and a plan change that the current usage exceeds is refused (plan-change-flow).
Jobs past a tenant's daily allowance are not admitted while another tenant's jobs run (job-admission-flow).
A feature flag is off for a tenant unless its release record enables it for that tenant (OPS-328).
Limits are data changed through an operation and take effect without a restart (AGT-420).
tasks.description: Component limit-store is "not-implemented". The spec has 41 per-source quotas, three plans (D-508), write-quota-flow, connection-quota-flow, job-admission-flow, plan-change-flow and one feature flag (OPS-328, AGT-420). Today the backend holds only per-source sign-in and socket caps in process. Resilience under pressure needs one tenant unable to starve another, with overload refused where it arrives (k-300).
tasks.title: Limit store enforces tenant quotas, plans and feature flags

acceptance_criteria: The PostgreSQL adapter passes every row of cases-storage-conformance that the SQLite adapter passes.

Provisioning creates a database, applies the layout and installs the template, and the directory reports the tenant active only after all three (TEN-002); a failed step rolls back (fm-provisioning-step-fails).
A layout change that fails on some tenant databases leaves each database either fully changed or unchanged and reports which (fm-bad-layout-change).
Export then restore into an empty store reproduces the tenant state (export-restore-flow).
Deleting a tenant removes its database, files and key, and can be cancelled inside the grace period (tenant-deletion-flow).
The stack runs in local containers without a cloud account (k-10).
tasks.description: Components postgres-adapter, tenant-database, control-plane and control-database are "not-implemented"; milestone rm-2 ("a tenant is a PostgreSQL database behind the store contract, found through a directory") is unmet. Only the SQLite adapter exists. Database-per-tenant in production, provisioning, suspension, export, deletion, restore and layout rollout all sit here.
tasks.title: PostgreSQL adapter, tenant directory and control plane

acceptance_criteria: A field declared personal is stored sealed and reads back in plain only for a reader whose policies permit it.
Erasing a subject destroys the subject's key, after which the sealed fields cannot be opened and stored copies are purged (erasure-copy-flow).
Every configuration and role change appends an audit entry with the previous value, new value, principal and correlation identifier (OPS-329).
verify-audit-chain detects an altered or removed entry.
export-subject-data returns every record that declares the subject as owner.
tasks.description: Components audit-log, key-service and subject-rights-service are "not-implemented". Profiles carry personal data, so the product spec needs k-350..352 to hold: personal fields declared, sealed under the subject's key, and the key destroyed on erasure (subject-key-flow, erasure-copy-flow, audit-chain-flow). Role and permission changes need the tamper-evident audit record (OPS-329).
tasks.title: Audit log and sealed personal fields

acceptance_criteria: The spec declares the ledger's records, contracts, claims and machines, and Exegra verify passes.
Posting the same entry twice with one idempotency key changes the balance once.
Two concurrent postings that together pass a declared cap result in exactly one refusal, and the balance never passes the cap.
A balance equals the sum of its entries after replaying the journal.
A product spec that declares a mutable balance outside the ledger is refused with a named rule; a negative fixture covers it.
tasks.description: Absent from the spec. The only counters are throttles. Points, badge progress, redemption limits and promotion budgets need an append-only ledger: entries with an idempotency key, balances derived from entries, and limits that hold under concurrent writes. Add it as a platform primitive with claims, a model machine and its implementation machine, then implement it in the kernel as a decision over declared records. Per the findings-become-refusals rule (WG-4948), add a rule refusing a product spec that keeps a mutable balance field outside the ledger.
tasks.title: Spec: a ledger primitive for points, caps and budgets

acceptance_criteria: The spec declares segment definitions, their contracts, claims and machines, and Exegra verify passes.
A person whose record changes to satisfy a segment's predicate produces one entry event in the transaction that commits the change, and one exit event when it stops satisfying it.
A segment's membership equals a fresh evaluation of its predicate over the tenant after replaying the journal.
A segment predicate reads only fields the definer's policies permit, and one that names another field is refused.
A predicate outside the declared expression language is refused at definition.
tasks.description: Absent from the spec. "Audience" there means the audience class of a read and the recipients of audience mail; nothing defines a saved predicate over principals and their records whose membership is kept current. Campaigns, promotions and targeted notifications need it. Add segments as tenant metadata in the declared expression language, with entry and exit as domain events that triggers can subscribe to.
tasks.title: Spec: segments, saved predicates over people that stay current

acceptance_criteria: The spec declares setting definitions with a type, a default and the levels allowed to override, with claims, and Exegra verify passes.
Reading a setting returns the most specific permitted override, and removing that override returns the next level's value.
An override at a level the definition does not allow, or of the wrong type, is refused.
A change to a setting is a domain event and reaches open pages over the live connection.
A product spec that reads configuration from anywhere but a declared setting is refused with a named rule; a negative fixture covers it.
tasks.description: Absent from the spec. Site settings exist as tenant data, and feature flags and quotas are tenant metadata, but nothing defines a typed setting with a default at the platform, an override at the tenant, the team and the person, and a rule for which level may override which. Deep configurability of product features needs it.
tasks.title: Spec: typed settings layered platform, tenant, team and person

acceptance_criteria: The spec declares count, sum and top-N over a named query's declared fields, with claims, and Exegra verify passes.
An aggregate result equals the same computation over the records the reader's policies permit, and counts no record the reader may not read.
An aggregate over an undeclared field is refused.
An aggregate that would scan past its declared bound is refused with a named error.
tasks.description: Named queries filter on declared fields (CMS-165) and nothing in the spec covers counts, sums or top-N. Leaderboards, badge progress, campaign results and unread counts need them, bounded so one tenant's query cannot starve the store.
tasks.title: Spec: aggregates in named queries

acceptance_criteria: The owner's decision is recorded as a decision in the spec, and ng-8 either stands with a stated reading or is reworded.
Exegra verify passes with the changed non-goal and decision.
tasks.description: ng-8 states "No built-in web analytics, email marketing or commerce." The incoming product spec names promotions and campaigns. Either the product spec's campaigns stay inside what the platform already allows (audience mail with unsubscribe, EML-020; no payments, ng-152), or ng-8 is narrowed. This is the owner's decision; it shapes the segments, ledger and mail tasks.
tasks.title: Decide: non-goal ng-8 against campaigns and promotions

acceptance_criteria: A workflow definition that names a trigger or action outside the published catalogue is refused at activation (INT-153).
A run started by a trigger advances through its steps, survives a worker restart between steps and applies each step's effect once.
A failed step runs the compensation of the completed steps in reverse order (workflow-compensation-flow).
A step that waits for approval continues only after a principal with workflow-approve approves it, and never on the approval of the principal who started it where the definition requires separation.
A run started under one definition version finishes under that version after a newer version is activated (workflow-version-flow).
tasks.description: Specified and modelled (workflow-definition-flow, workflow-activation-flow, workflow-run-flow, workflow-compensation-flow, approval-flow, call-step-flow, workflow-version-flow) with contracts activate-workflow, start-workflow-run, advance-workflow-run and approve-workflow-step, but nothing runs them. This is the rule layer of the product spec: automation is workflows over declared step kinds and calls to external addresses (D-506, ng-3), with no tenant code.
tasks.title: Workflow runs: definitions, activation, steps, approval and compensation

acceptance_criteria: A notice sent to a person appears in that person's inbox and in no one else's, and reaches their open page over the live connection.
The spec declares notification kinds, channels and per-person preferences with claims, and Exegra verify passes.
A person who turns a kind off for a channel receives none of that kind on that channel, while a kind the tenant marks required is still delivered.
Notices of a kind set to digest are delivered once per period as one message listing them.
An inbox item ends at the point ret-inbox-item states.
tasks.description: Component notification-service is "not-implemented". Contracts send-notice, list-inbox and subscribe-notifications and the machine approval-inbox-flow exist. The spec has no per-person preference by notification kind and channel and no digest; the only opt-out is the mail unsubscribe (EML-020). Add those to the spec, then run the service over the existing live connection and the job runner.
tasks.title: Notification service: inbox, live delivery, preferences and digests

acceptance_criteria: A request to send mail becomes a job in the transaction that commits its change (EML-005), and a rolled-back change sends nothing.
A message to a suppressed address is not sent, and a hard-bounce delivery report adds the address to the suppression list.
Mail past the tenant's monthly allowance is held and other tenants' mail is sent (mail-quota-flow).
Mail to an audience carries the unsubscribe header and a link that takes effect without a sign-in (EML-020).
A template renders token values as text in their output context (k-450), and tenant content cannot inject markup.
Every row of cases-mail-conformance passes against a local adapter that needs no cloud account.
tasks.description: Components mail-service and mail-dispatcher are "not-implemented"; sign-in links are the only mail today. Specified and modelled: mail-enqueue-flow, mail-attempt-flow, mail-quota-flow, mail-provider-flow, mail-render-flow, sender-domain-flow, delivery-report-flow, audience-mail-flow, with cases-mail-conformance. The dispatcher is the one component that talks to a mail provider (k-451).
tasks.title: Mail dispatcher with templates, suppression, quotas and delivery reports

acceptance_criteria: A call to a loopback, private or link-local address that a tenant names is refused by the gate, including after a redirect and after a DNS answer that changes.
A webhook delivery is signed, retried with backoff on failure, and the tenant sees each delivery's response status and attempt count (INT-152).
An inbound webhook with a wrong or replayed signature is refused, and an accepted one starts its run once.
A response past the size or time bound is cut off and recorded as such (outbound-call-flow).
tasks.description: Components outbound-gate, connector-runner and external-endpoint are "not-implemented". Specified and modelled: outbound-call-flow, webhook-delivery-flow, inbound-signature-flow, inbound-run-flow, call-step-flow. Every connection to an address a tenant names leaves through one gate (k-252, D-702). This is how a product feature reaches anything outside the declared step kinds.
tasks.title: Outbound gate, webhook delivery and inbound webhooks

acceptance_criteria: specc turns a product spec into a bundle file, and installing the same bundles into an empty store produces the same tenant state (RUN-004).
A bundle that contains anything but declared metadata is refused (INT-155).
A tenant installs a bundle only after its projection has been shown, and the installed result equals the projection (INT-154).
A module's operations reach tenant data only through the runtime (ARC-112), and installing it changes no kernel code (ARC-113).
Upgrading an installed module to a newer bundle version is offered as a proposal and applies as a schema change with its migration.
tasks.description: Contracts install-bundle and parse-bundle and the machine template-install-flow exist; component product-module is "not-implemented". A product module compiled from a product spec must become a bundle of declared metadata (record types, views, workflows, operations, settings, roles) that a tenant installs through kernel intents after reviewing its projection.
tasks.title: Bundle install: a product module lands in a tenant as reviewed metadata

acceptance_criteria: The badges product spec passes Exegra verify and installs into a tenant as a bundle.
The commits that add it change nothing under crates/kernel and add no hand-written route or handler.

Generated journeys pass in the browser suite: an owner defines a badge; a person who meets the rule is awarded it once however often the rule fires; the person sees it and gets an inbox notice; a person without the permission cannot define or award one.
A second tenant on the same process that has not installed the module has none of its record types, views or operations.
The scoped check for this module finishes in under 120 s (measured).
tasks.description: The proof that the layering works before the large product spec arrives. Write badges as a product spec in its own file: a badge definition record type, an award rule as a workflow started by a trigger, progress and caps on the ledger, an inbox notice on award, a view of a person's badges, and the permissions to define and award. It adds no platform mechanism.
tasks.title: Reference feature: badges built as a product module from primitives only

acceptance_criteria: The spec declares each workflow step kind with its inputs, outputs, effect and compensation, and each trigger with the domain event or schedule it fires on, as entities a product spec can refer to by id; Exegra validate passes.
INT-153's refusal is stated against those entities: a definition naming an id that is not a declared step kind or trigger is refused, shown by a scenario.
The generated capability catalogue lists the step kinds and triggers.
A product spec whose workflow names an undeclared step kind is refused with a named rule; a negative fixture covers it.
tasks.description: Found while building the capability catalogue (WG-4990): D-506 says a workflow is made of the step kinds the platform declares, and INT-153 refuses a definition that names a trigger or action outside "the published catalogue", but no type, record or contract lists the step kinds, the triggers or the actions. They exist only as prose and as the events of the workflow, trigger and step machines. A product spec cannot compose workflows from a list that is not written down, and activation cannot be checked against it.
tasks.title: Spec: declare workflow step kinds and triggers as data

acceptance_criteria: A product file declaring a record type with fields, references and policies passes Exegra validate, and is reported as a tenant object type, not a platform table.
A product file declaring an operation over its record types, with auth, inputs, outputs and errors, passes validate with a realisation meaning interpreted tenant metadata.

A product operation whose body uses anything outside the declared expression language or the declared step kinds is refused with a named rule that says what to use instead; a negative fixture covers it.
A product claim or scenario that asserts about a platform entity's behaviour is refused with a named rule; a negative fixture covers it.
The Strata fixture product is extended with a record type and an operation and still leaves every platform-generated file byte-identical.
tasks.description: Found by WG-4989. A product file can be layered on the platform spec, but its two central kinds do not fit the format yet. A product `record` is read as a fixed platform table, which Exegra's rule record.tenant-data-fixed and claim ARC-113 forbid. A product contract fails ready.contract-realisation-missing because no realisation value means "interpreted from tenant metadata". So the Strata fixture product holds only types, a role and a claim. Before the large product spec lands, the format needs: a record scope meaning a tenant object type installed as metadata, a contract realisation meaning an operation interpreted by the runtime from metadata (no generated or hand-written handler), and specc output for them (the bundle, WG-5007).
tasks.title: A product spec can declare record types and operations as tenant metadata

acceptance_criteria: Each of the nine areas has a findings list where every finding names a file and line (or spec entity id), the evidence, and a concrete failure scenario
Every finding rated high is re-checked by the coordinator against the source before it is reported
Each confirmed finding is filed as a Workgraph task with testable acceptance criteria, or recorded on an existing task that already covers it
tasks.description: Read-only audit of the integration line (strata-int3-kernel, branch stackp) and the Exegra layering branch. Nine areas, one agent each: kernel and storage; runtime, backend and substrate; BFF and web application; spec compiler; spec security and tenancy; spec composition for product modules; spec against code; tooling and tests; resilience under load. Findings are verified by the coordinator and filed as tasks.
tasks.title: Audit the whole Strata platform for gaps and likely problems: spec, code and tooling

acceptance_criteria: A test parses 200,000 '>' characters and returns without overflowing the stack, with nesting cut at a stated maximum depth
A test parses 200,000 '[' characters within a stated time bound
/api/preview requires a session or a per-source rate limit, shown by a test that is refused without it
word_count and serialisation of a document at the maximum depth do not overflow
A spec claim states the maximum Markdown nesting depth and field length, with a negative fixture
tasks.description: Confirmed in source. crates/substrate/src/markdown.rs:250-261 recurses once per leading '>' with no depth cap. crates/bff/src/routes.rs:1260-1283 (/api/preview) parses up to 200,000 characters with only an Origin check, no session; a stack overflow aborts the process. The same parser runs on tenant record fields at every view render (substrate/src/project.rs). Inline parsing is also quadratic (markdown.rs:99-100, 143-146). From WG-5014, runtime audit findings 1-2 and web audit finding 11.
tasks.title: Markdown parser: one request of nested quotes crashes the process for every tenant

acceptance_criteria: With one tenant file corrupted, a test shows other tenants' events are still published and their sessions still listed
An event row that fails to decode is parked and reported, and later events of that tenant and all events of other tenants are published
A tenant with more pending events than the batch limit does not delay another tenant's events beyond one sweep
The Store trait has a per-tenant, per-principal session query and no request path calls the all-tenant scan
Open tenant handles are bounded by a configured maximum, shown by a test that touches more tenants than the bound
Opening a cold tenant does not block a call for an already open tenant
Liveness answers without opening any tenant file; the integrity check is not reachable by a tenant or an unauthenticated caller
tasks.description: Confirmed in source. crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs: outbox (1410-1440) returns Err on the first tenant file that will not open or the first event that will not decode, and fills its limit from the first tenants in id order; live_sessions (1532-1548) loads every tenant's sessions and is called by 'list my sessions', role assignment and SCIM (backend/src/auth.rs:413-420, ops.rs:42-50); tenant_db (856-871) holds one global lock across the control query, file open and migrations, and never evicts; health() runs quick_check on every tenant and is reachable unauthenticated and from tenant diagnostics. backend/src/hub.rs:244-253 returns early on one tenant's load error. From WG-5014: resilience findings 1-6, kernel findings 4-5, runtime findings 5 and 12.
tasks.title: SQLite store: one broken tenant must not stop outbox, sessions, health or purges for all tenants

acceptance_criteria: A test updates one scalar field of a record holding a list of 100 references and succeeds
The number of store loads for that update is bounded by a constant, asserted in the test
A schema change touching more than 32 referenced object types succeeds or is refused with a named limit, not InsufficientState
tasks.description: Confirmed in source. kernel/src/transition.rs:173-181 needs() pre-loads only references and unique values of the supplied fields; rules.rs validate_record looks up every reference and unique field of the whole candidate; storage-api/src/lib.rs:938-980 adds one missing need per round and stops at MAX_NEED_ROUNDS = 32. Large ChangeSchema migrations hit the same limit. From WG-5014 kernel finding 1.
tasks.title: Kernel: updating a record that holds many references is refused after 32 reload rounds

acceptance_criteria: A member manager who lacks Manage Schema cannot assign, invite to, or add to a team holding a role whose policy grants Manage Schema; test for each of the three paths
Revoking a role or removing a team member is refused unless the actor could confer that role
No sequence of direct or team revocations leaves a tenant with zero effective owners
An invitation has an expiry and a revoke intent, and redemption re-checks the creator's authority
An unauthorized caller gets the same error for an existing and a missing record id
The spec states the revocation rule and specc or Exegra refuses a spec that lacks it, with a negative fixture
tasks.description: Confirmed in source for conferral: kernel/src/rules.rs:168-199 may_confer compares only schema.grants_of(role) (role_permissions, schema.rs:157), while authorize also grants through schema.policies (rules.rs:285), so a role empowered by a policy 'grants nothing' and anyone with Manage Members can assign it. Agent-reported, not re-checked: revoke paths (transition.rs:759-813, 887-965) need only Manage Members; the last-owner check covers direct members only, so revoking owner through a team can leave zero owners; invitations never expire, cannot be revoked and are not re-checked at redemption (transition.rs:967-1097); authorization happens after existence lookups (transition.rs:560, 690, 405). Spec side: ADM-152 limits only assigning; no define-role or define-team contract. From WG-5014 kernel findings 2, 11, 12, 13 and spec security findings 7, 19.
tasks.title: Kernel: role conferral ignores policies, and revocation needs no authority over the role

acceptance_criteria: A conformance check for every store: a session revoked after it was read stays revoked when the stale copy is written back
last-seen and authenticated-at are updated by a write that cannot change revoked_at
The step-up confirm path passes the same check
tasks.description: Reported independently by two agents, not re-checked by the coordinator. backend/src/auth.rs:213-216 reads the session and, when it is over 60 s stale, writes the whole record back; storage-sqlite put_session (1476-1505) upserts revoked_at from the stale copy. A revoke landing between read and write is undone. signin/stepup.rs:145-148 has the same read-modify-write. From WG-5014 kernel finding 6 and runtime finding 3.
tasks.title: A revoked session can be revived by the last-seen write

acceptance_criteria: specc refuses a non-local contract with no tenantScope, with a negative fixture
Under scope request, a principal with no tenant is refused; generated test
Scopes none and platform each have a generated check or specc refuses them
tenantPolicies is either enforced by generated code or refused by specc
The spec states that an explicit tenant input must equal the resolved tenant and every such contract lists the error; a rule refuses a public contract with a tenant input that lacks it
The search contract no longer accepts an audience from the caller
tasks.description: Confirmed in source. spec-compiler/src/backend/routes.rs:1539-1546: the generated authorizer checks the tenant only when tenant_scope == Some(Request), and then a principal with no tenant passes for any site. 156 of 340 contracts declare no tenantScope and nothing refuses that; 'none' and 'platform' are carried but not enforced; auth.tenantPolicies appears only in doc text. Spec side (confirmed): 64 public contracts take a tenant-id input while GWY-001 says the tenant comes from the host alone, and the outcome when they differ is unspecified; search (CT-175) takes its audience class from the anonymous caller. From WG-5014 specc finding 1 and spec security findings 1, 12.
tasks.title: specc: tenant scope must be required and enforced on every non-local contract

acceptance_criteria: A type with pattern [a-z]{3} rejects 'abc!!!' in generated Rust and in the page; test
A spec or product file with a duplicate object key is refused with its line; negative fixture
Duplicate role, capability, plan, grant and flag ids are each refused; negative fixtures
Two generated files with one path are refused for every specc command
Every specc command runs the shared readiness check before emitting
Equality on option<list<T>> agrees between the Rust and JavaScript targets in the expression conformance cases
Catalogue output escapes table and link syntax; fixture with '|' in a description
tasks.description: Confirmed in source: backend/types.rs:1375-1387 emits Regex::new(p).is_match for a type's constraints.pattern with no anchoring (field patterns use rules::anchored); jsonc.rs:35-41 parses through serde_json Value, which keeps the last duplicate key silently. Agent-reported: roles, capabilities, plans, grants and flags have no duplicate-id check and lookups take the first (load.rs:1058-1158, access_model.rs); a client machine or language named like a kernel file or backend module overwrites it (web.rs:112, language.rs:831); same-source duplicate ids pass Claims (codetext.rs:143-153); 'specc web', e2e, catalogue and deploy skip readiness; JS equality is by reference for option<list>, option<named> and bytes (spec-expr/src/js.rs:541-553); diagnostics carry no line; catalogue text is not Markdown-escaped. From WG-5014 specc findings 2, 3, 5-10, 13, 16.
tasks.title: specc: refuse duplicate keys and ids, anchor type patterns, reserve generated file names

acceptance_criteria: Negative fixtures in specc and Exegra for each: product role at platform level, product role with anonymous or service holder, product contract public and anonymous, product contract implemented by a platform component, duplicate product id, malformed product entity id
A platform reference to a product entity is refused in both tools
A reference to a platform entity through from, to, contract, record or target requires an import
Exegra reload picks up a changed product file; test
tasks.description: Agent-reported, not re-checked. spec-compiler/src/layers.rs checks product sections for id redefinition and imports only, then discards them: a product role may use level platform or anonymous/service holders; a product contract may use exposure public with scheme anonymous or implementedBy a platform component; two product files may share a product id; entity ids are not pattern-checked; import detection walks only type, repr, capabilities and requires. Exegra side (exegra src/core/layers.js:518-521): a platform entity referencing a product entity raises no diagnostic; project.js reload() ignores changed product files. Follows WG-4989. From WG-5014 specc findings 4, 11, 12 and tooling findings 18, 23.
tasks.title: Layering: refuse product entities that claim platform powers

acceptance_criteria: The export excludes or re-seals credentials, sessions and challenges, and a claim says how an import treats them
Export, restore, deletion, support-grant issue and owner-role assignment require step-up, and a rule refuses a contract in the sensitive list without it
Platform flags and quotas need a capability no tenant role holds; plan change has a billing gate and error cases
Each platform component has its own capability set; the audit actor is derived, not supplied
A claim states that catalogue invocation enforces the underlying contract's capability and roles, with a negative scenario
A claim states which identity and authorization state a restore keeps revoked
Audit retention has a floor and the chain has a head checkpoint that survives expiry
Exegra validates with no new errors
tasks.description: Confirmed in spec: copy-tenant-export includes rec-credential, rec-session, rec-challenge, rec-grant, rec-provider-config, rec-connector-secret, rec-delivery-key, and export-tenant needs only an owner session with no step-up; flags-manage is held by both owner and platform-operator. Agent-reported: change-plan lets an owner pick any plan; platform-service is one role with 13 capabilities and append-audit-entry takes a caller-supplied actor; catalogue invocation (CT-110) states no capability check; support grants lack purpose, scope and expiry bound; restore-tenant has no rule for revoked sessions, grants and role assignments; delete-tenant has no request contract, step-up or notice; step-up coverage does not match D-4915; audit retention can be shortened to 30 days and truncation is undetectable; restore windows disagree (DEP-011, OPS-320, D-522). From WG-5014 spec security findings 3-6, 8, 10, 14-17.
tasks.title: Spec: owner-level operations that expose or destroy everything need tighter rules

acceptance_criteria: The spec defines each lifecycle state and what a tenant in it may still do, including serving content, jobs, mail and sessions
An operator contract takes a tenant or host down, with a stated bound on how long gateways keep serving it
A tenant is created at runtime without a restart, and its owner receives a first login; test
An install interrupted after its first commit is resumed or rolled back on the next start; test
One failing bundle does not prevent other tenants from starting; test
Fork has claims for isolation, lifetime and erasure propagation
tasks.description: Agent-reported. Code: tenants exist only from bundle files at process start (backend/src/seed.rs); a partial install is never repaired and one bad bundle stops startup (substrate/src/bundle.rs:487-560, backend/src/lib.rs:38-45); the directory knows only active and deleting; the BFF host map is a static environment variable; no production path gives a new tenant's owner a login. Spec: suspension refuses only state-changing requests, so an abusive tenant's site, jobs and mail keep running; directory copies are served for 15 minutes; no operator takedown contract; fork-tenant has no claims; sandbox and move have gaps. Related: WG-4996. From WG-5014 resilience findings 10, 23; runtime finding 16; web finding 6; spec security findings 2, 14, 23, 24.
tasks.title: Tenant lifecycle: provision, suspend, take down, delete, restore and fork are unspecified or unbuilt

acceptance_criteria: A named query over 100,000 records with limit 20 loads a number of records bounded by a constant, asserted in a test
Every list read takes a cursor and has a stated maximum page size
Record, field, list and schema sizes have stated maximums in the spec, enforced by the kernel, each with a refusal test
A create retried with the same idempotency key yields one record; conformance check for every store
A policy or filter that follows a reference evaluates on a real partial snapshot; test not using World
One record that fails a filter does not fail the query for other rows
tasks.description: Reported independently by three agents. kernel/src/read.rs:85-207: every named query loads and decodes every record of the object type, filters and sorts in memory, then applies an optional limit; no cursor; no cap on ids in a records read. No limit on string length, list length, record count, fields per type, or changes per schema change (rules.rs:397-531). Members and schema are single JSON blobs rewritten on every member change (storage-sqlite 426-459, 1056-1121). No idempotency key in Intent or Context, so a retried create duplicates (storage-api/src/lib.rs:117-123); a 408 does not cancel the blocking write (runtime/src/server.rs:158-224). Rules that follow a reference fail on reads because reads have no need-retry loop (read.rs:47-82); one grandfathered bad record fails a whole query (read.rs:170-174). Spec: CMS-255's plan bound is stated nowhere. From WG-5014 kernel findings 7-9, 14, 15, 17; resilience findings 8, 9; composition finding F15, F24.
tasks.title: Reads and writes need bounds: paging, pushdown, size limits, idempotency keys

acceptance_criteria: With one tenant saturated by slow reads, another tenant's request completes within a stated bound; test
A flood on the token endpoint cannot run more concurrent Argon2 verifications than the configured permit count; test
A hung identity provider does not block password sign-in; test
A burst of 2,000 events in one tenant closes no socket of another tenant; test
A client resuming with 500 missed events is not disconnected; test
A Lab run reads only the requesting tenant
The spec defines source address derivation and has quota entries for signed and authenticated expensive contracts
tasks.description: Agent-reported. No per-tenant or global in-flight limit; all store calls share the blocking pool and each tenant has one connection behind a mutex (runtime/src/server.rs:216, runtime/src/sqlite.rs:82-132). Argon2 permits are process-wide and held across the OIDC callback's network call (backend/src/http.rs:98-108); the token endpoint hashes outside admission control (http.rs:713-722, service/clients.rs:178-211). One 1024-slot broadcast carries every tenant's events (hub.rs:60-69); resume replay can overflow the 256-slot socket queue (ws.rs:213-228); no per-connection message rate (ws.rs:250-307). Rate tables refuse every new source once 20,000 keys are held (runtime/src/limits.rs:97-120). Lab runs load every tenant into memory (lab.rs:490-495). Mail spawns a thread per message (mail.rs:148-156). Spec: quotas cover only anonymous contracts by source address, and source address is undefined. From WG-5014 resilience findings 7, 12-15, 18, 22; runtime findings 4, 9-11, 13, 23, 28; spec security findings 11, 20, 26.
tasks.title: One tenant can starve the rest: add per-tenant limits to requests, hashing, events and rate tables

acceptance_criteria: An identity provider asserting a verified email outside its domains cannot link to an existing account; test
Linking an identity and each owner-level service operation is refused without recent authentication; tests
First enrolment of a required second factor needs proof beyond the password
A person deactivated during a pending sign-in gets no session
The signing key is sealed at rest and the factor key is separate, required and versioned; a rotation test keeps existing authenticators working
An invitation is redeemable by an account whose address was proved by an emailed link or a trusted provider; test
Two concurrent SCIM creates of one userName yield one account and one conflict
tasks.description: Agent-reported, not re-checked. Linking by verified email ignores the provider's domains list (signin/federated.rs:251-264); linking a federated identity needs no step-up (signin/oidc/mod.rs:132-142, saml/mod.rs:210-220); a required second factor can be self-enrolled with only the password (signin/second.rs:121-135); the disabled check is skipped at the second-factor step (second.rs:177-275); role assignment, signing-key rotation, client and provisioning-token creation need no step-up; the tenant's token-signing private key is stored in plaintext (service/keys.rs:9-12); the TOTP seal key defaults to the service token the BFF also holds, with no key id (main.rs:94-109); verified_email is set only for dev accounts, so invitations cannot be redeemed in production; put_account is an unconditional upsert (storage-sqlite 2489-2508); timing separates password-less accounts (auth.rs:279-287); SCIM throttles before checking the token. From WG-5014 runtime findings 4a, 7, 8, 14, 15, 17, 21, 25-27; kernel finding 19; drift finding 19.
tasks.title: Identity hardening: federated linking, step-up coverage, key storage, invitations in production

acceptance_criteria: Every authentication decision is written durably per tenant and survives a restart; test
The platform diagnostics route requires an operator identity and writes an audit entry
Dev routes are absent from a build without the development feature; test on the route table
A non-dev start with no sites, no mail sink or a missing factor key refuses to start with a named reason; tests
The BFF token survives a restart and validates across two instances; test
SIGTERM drains connections within a stated deadline
Journal and event retention is stated in the spec and a verified address is not written to the journal
Every environment variable and BFF route is declared in the spec, checked by the gate
tasks.description: Agent-reported by several agents. Authentication decisions and audit entries live in one shared 1,000-entry in-memory ring (backend/src/app.rs:275-303). /internal/platform/diagnostics reads every tenant with only the shared service token (http.rs:511, 1037); tenant diagnostics leak cross-tenant counts and failing tenant ids. Dev routes (/internal/dev/reset, clock, identity-outage and others) are compiled into every build and gated by STRATA_DEV at run time; dev accounts with published passwords install when it is set. Unconfigured production start serves demo tenants on loopback hosts (bff/src/main.rs:59-77) and sends mail to an in-memory sink (backend/src/main.rs:59-78). The BFF request-token secret is random per process (bff/src/token.rs:43-47). STRATA_TRUSTED_PROXIES defaults to empty. Only Ctrl-C is handled for shutdown. Journals store verified addresses and full before/after records forever (kernel finding 16). About 40 environment variables and 30 BFF routes are not in the spec. The production backend can shell out to lake. Related: WG-4997. From WG-5014 runtime findings 6, 14, 20, 24; web findings 1, 6, 12-16; resilience findings 16, 19-21, 24; drift findings 7-9, 22-24; tooling findings 3, 22.
tasks.title: Production safety: durable audit, operator routes, dev switches and startup defaults

acceptance_criteria: A differential test runs the hand-written kernel and the generated kernel functions on the spec's scenarios and fails on any difference, or the kernel calls the generated functions
The backend's session and throttle logic is checked against the spec machines' traces

tasks.description: Confirmed in source: kernel_transition and kernel_read (model-core/src/functions.rs, model/src/derived.rs) have no caller outside generated code; the backend runs the hand-written strata_kernel and no test compares the two; strata_model::quotas is not referenced by backend, bff or runtime. Agent-reported: the session and throttle machines are generated but the backend's hand-written auth runs; session lifetime in code is 2 h idle / 12 h absolute (backend/src/main.rs:197-198, confirmed) while d-700 says 12 h / 14 days; components marked manual hide about 45 public contracts with no handler; identity-service is marked not-implemented but is largely built, with 13 tables that have no spec record; 118 of 860 requirements are named by any test, 1 of 65 in tenancy; 784 claims are labelled realisation checked; 13 of 22 tested property claims use no generator; the Lean model is a smaller system than the kernel. From WG-5014 drift findings 1-6, 14-16, 21, 25.
tasks.title: The spec's assurances must be about the code that runs

tasks.description: Confirmed in source: system-differential/tests/exegra.rs:728 stops comparing a scenario when both sides fail at one step, unplannable scenarios are only printed, and the final assertion needs just one covered scenario (866-884); verification/src/obligations.rs:61 cites strata-kernel::properties::outsiders_cannot_mutate, which does not exist, and correspondence.rs checks only theorem names; storage-sqlite/tests/recorded_data.rs:220-231 overwrites its goldens and passes when STRATA_RECORD is set. Agent-reported: the gate runs no browser tests, no client tests, no generated journeys, no clippy, fmt, cargo audit or npm audit, and has no child timeouts; there is no CI configuration; e2e runs with --no-build against whatever binaries exist; --allow-recorded trusts a boolean the gate wrote; Exegra records a skipped Playwright test as a pass (cli/commands.js:468-478); hmr.spec.js rewrites tracked source files; several kernel and verification tests have holes (properties.rs:465, behaviour.rs:1169, purity.rs:172, state_machine.rs:199); no crash, upgrade, backup or many-tenant test exists; model and model-core do not inherit the unsafe_code forbid. Related: WG-4991. From WG-5014 tooling findings 2, 4-17, 19, 21; drift findings 10-13, 17, 18.
tasks.title: Checks that can pass without checking: differential, obligations, goldens, gate coverage

acceptance_criteria: A product file declares 'on event X, when condition C, do A, wait D, then B, retry with policy P' using only platform entities, shown by a fixture that specc accepts

A declined or parked job produces a record the tenant owner can list
Claims state hop counting across delays, ordering between a subscriber's jobs, and the outcome when the job quota is exceeded at commit
tasks.description: Confirmed in spec: no define-trigger contract exists and tenant-schema has no triggers member (its members are version, objects, roles, role-permissions, teams, invitations, policies, workflows, queries, views). Agent-reported: INT-153 refuses actions 'outside the published catalogue' but no catalogue is defined; define-schedule has no target; schedule-job takes a kind with no handler registry; workflow-def is one field's state machine and the effect union has only publish and revoke-sessions; no claim says which principal a trigger-created job acts as; the hop limit of eight counts ledger and segment events and a declined job leaves no trace; ordering after a parked event is unspecified; a job past the daily quota may refuse the commit that creates it. tasks.title: Automation cannot be expressed: triggers, step catalogue, delays, run-as authority

acceptance_criteria: A fixture product declares 'redeem a promotion': one operation that checks segment membership and a ledger limit, posts to the ledger and creates a record, committed together
The rule language has integer arithmetic and time arithmetic with the same checked semantics in Rust and JavaScript
A rule can read the acting person's ledger balance, segment membership and resolved setting; fixture for each
A member can read their own balance and membership without a capability that exposes others'
A policy can restrict ledger reads by owner
A ranked balance listing exists with a stated bound
The spec states whether segment batch jobs count against the job quota, and offers refresh on change
Decisions D-5000 and D-5021 no longer contradict
tasks.description: Confirmed in spec: the tenant rule language has no arithmetic (operators: lit, var, through, param, now, principal, has-role, or, and, not, cmp, in, is-null, len, lower, contains, starts-with, is-slug, if); ledger-post is held by owner only. Agent-reported: no intent carries a record change together with ledger postings, although LDG-009 and D-5013 require them to commit together; segment membership, ledger balance and settings are not in any expression scope, so policies, guards, queries and views cannot read them; D-5021's workaround (a maintained counter field) contradicts D-5000; a policy cannot name ledger entries, members cannot read their own balance or segment membership, and there is no account listing, ranking or expiry; segments key on principals only; a time-dependent segment of 10,000 people at a 60 s refresh uses the whole default job admission rate; the cap is 25 segments per tenant; setting-changed carries no value and the dispatcher cannot resolve a recipient's preference; no composite unique constraint. Extends WG-5011. From WG-5014 composition findings F2-F5, F11-F14, F27, F28, F30.
tasks.title: Primitives do not connect: ledger, segments and settings are unreachable from rules, operations and members

acceptance_criteria: A workflow step sends a templated mail or inbox notice to a principal, an address or a segment with an idempotency key; fixture
Inbox items can be marked read and removed, and a digest step exists
Suppression and preferences are per category, and transactional mail is not blocked by a marketing unsubscribe
A send carries a campaign reference that the mail log and an aggregate can report on
The spec defines the recurrence format and a tenant and person time zone
A product can declare a domain event and a trigger can select on event kind
tasks.description: Agent-reported. submit-message, send-notice and render-message are local; no tenant-facing contract or workflow step sends mail or creates an inbox notice. Inbox: topics are free strings, the read flag has no setter, no remove, digest, mute or quiet hours. No contract binds a segment to a send although D-5020 and D-5080 rely on it. Suppression is per address with no category, so unsubscribing from marketing blocks transactional mail; mail quota has two classes; the mail log carries no campaign or template, so measurement is impossible. No time zone anywhere and the recurrence format is undefined. Only 10 domain events exist and a selector filters by object type only; a product cannot declare its own event. Related: WG-5004, WG-5005. From WG-5014 composition findings F6, F7, F20-F22.
tasks.title: Messaging and notifications: no product-callable send, thin inbox, one suppression list

acceptance_criteria: One bundle install creates record types, segments, settings, ledger units and limits, templates and tokens as one projected change; fixture
A product can be upgraded and removed, and removal finds every entity it owns
A tenant field declares a personal-data kind and a type declares retention; subject export and erasure reach them and the search index; scenarios
Field-level read is evaluated by the kernel on reads; test with a public and a private field on one record
A file reference field type exists and file privacy follows the referring record's policy
A product file may declare capabilities, and a member-level capability exists for self-service writes
Publish, withdraw and scheduled publish are contracts usable for any content type; a language field and tenant fallback exist
D-103 and the layer rules agree on whether a product may register platform code
One naming and one pagination convention across primitives, enforced by a rule
tasks.description: Agent-reported. install-bundle writes only what schema-change covers; segments, settings, ledger units and limits, mail templates and tokens each need a separate owner call, and there is no uninstall, upgrade, product ownership of ids or platform-version field. aggregate-def and setting-def exist but nothing references them (these were deferred to the kernel work in commit 3530957). Tenant fields cannot declare a personal-data kind or retention, so export, erasure and sealing cannot reach product data; field-def.read exists but no function evaluates it; erasure does not reach the search index. No file reference field type; upload is one call with no size cap and needs content-write. A product cannot declare capabilities, and member self-service needs capabilities that also allow authoring. Content: no publish, withdraw or schedule contract, review is not connected to workflow runs, and localisation has no language field or fallback entity. D-103 allows 'platform code it registers' while NG-3 and the layer rules forbid it. Idempotency, concurrency parameter names and pagination differ across primitives. Related: WG-5007. From WG-5014 composition findings F8, F9, F16-F19, F24, F25; spec security findings 9, 13, 18.
tasks.title: Product data model gaps: bundle install, personal data, field reads, files, capabilities, content

acceptance_criteria: After sign-out and sign-in as another person on one tab, no recovery code, secret, draft or list of the first person is in the worker state; browser test
A change committed between page render and socket subscription appears on the page; browser test
After a frame gap the view is refetched; test
A refused socket upgrade refreshes the token or stops retrying; test
A 404 under /assets/ is not cacheable; test
Adding a screen to the spec needs no hand edit in navigation, guards or the BFF; shown by a fixture screen
The production bundle contains no source maps and no debug hook
tasks.description: Agent-reported, not re-checked. Sign-out and account switch do not clear the worker's per-user state: recovery codes, TOTP enrolment secret, session and passkey lists, Lab results and unsaved drafts stay for the next person on the tab (web/src/kernel/update.js:386, 510-527). Three ways to miss live updates with the footer still saying Live (update.js:352, 370; backend ws.rs:210). The reconnect loop reuses an expired token forever (web/src/worker/main.js:79-81). Every /assets/ response, including 404 and 5xx, is cached immutable for a year (bff/src/routes.rs:1622-1626). Navigation, guards, row actions and the BFF title logic are hard-coded to the publication's views (view.js:94, 261-266; shell.js:17-56; routes.rs:1125-1165, 1505-1513). The click handler captures links to /keys, /scim and /api (main.js:128-134). Source maps are served publicly. A debug socket hook ships in the bundle. Every keystroke re-renders and clones the whole model. From WG-5014 web findings 2-5, 7-9, 13, 17-21; tooling finding 24.
tasks.title: Web client and BFF: state kept across sign-out, missed live updates, blog-shaped hard-coding

acceptance_criteria: Deleting a record referenced from two fields of one record clears both; test
A schema change that rewrites records bumps their version and emits an event per record
An update is authorized against the final candidate after workflow assignments
A lock longer than its window lasts its full length; test
The team: prefix is refused for principal ids
A binary refuses to open a tenant database whose migration ledger is newer than it knows; test
A fleet migration command reports per-tenant status and stops at a stated failure share
A bundle path that leaves the tenant directory is refused; test
tasks.description: Agent-reported, not re-checked. Deleting a record referenced by two fields of one record leaves a dangling reference (kernel/src/transition.rs:699-744). RemoveField rewrites records with no version bump or event (transition.rs:1310-1325). Update policies see the candidate before workflow set assignments (transition.rs:574-649). A throttle lock is cut short by its window (storage-api/src/lib.rs:283-309). A team and a user can share a principal id (team: prefix). Unique lookups scan for values over 240 bytes. The adapter trusts the delta. Tenant bundles can read files outside their directory (protocol/src/tenants.rs:63-86). Platform upgrades migrate each tenant at first touch with no waves, no refusal when the ledger is newer than the binary, and no checksum. A cached connection can outlive its tenant; lock poisoning is permanent; restore_snapshot rewinds event sequence numbers. Optimistic retry has no backoff. From WG-5014 kernel findings 3, 10, 18, 20-24; resilience findings 17, 25-30.
tasks.title: Kernel and store correctness: delete with two references, migrations without events, throttle lock, fleet upgrades
