tasks.description: D-6525 and WFL-1527 say every intent of an automated step is decided with the principal automation:<workflow-id> holding exactly the roles of AutomationDef.run_as. The kernel has no such principal: spec type principal is system, anonymous or user, and crates/kernel/src/rules.rs roles_of resolves a user through members and teams only. Where it attaches: either a principal variant automation(workflow-id) or a reserved prefix automation: refused for persons as team: is in transition.rs refuse_reserved_principals; roles_of must then return the run-as roles from TenantSchema.automations (plus public). The worker of WG-4992 maps each AutomationStep variant (crates/model-core generated, held in schema.automations) to an Intent: create-record, update-record and delete-record to the record intents, branch to an evaluation; the step key of D-6528 goes in Context.idempotency_key. Removing an automation must leave its principal with no roles.
tasks.title: Kernel: decide automation steps as the automation principal automation:<workflow-id> with its run-as roles

acceptance_criteria: A kernel test: revoking the editor role of the definer of an automation whose run-as is editor marks the automation suspended in the same transition
Defining the automation again as a principal who may confer every run-as role clears the suspension, shown by a test
The defined-by member is written by the kernel from the context and a supplied value is ignored, shown by a test
tasks.description: D-6526, D-6527 and WFL-1529 need the definer of an automation: its runs name the definer as on-behalf-of, and a change of the definer's roles, team roles, role permissions or erasure suspends an automation whose run-as the definer can no longer confer (contract recheck-automation-authority, CT-798). WG-5045 checks the run-as at definition (transition.rs require_definition_authority with may_confer) but automation-def has no defined-by member, so nothing can be rechecked. Where it attaches: add defined-by (principal-id, set by change_schema from ctx.principal, never from the input) and a suspended flag to automation-def in specifications/spec.jsonc; in transition.rs change_member, team_role, team_member and DefineRolePermissions, re-run may_confer for each automation the affected principals defined and mark it suspended in the same delta.
tasks.title: Kernel: record the definer of an automation and suspend it when the definer loses authority (WFL-1529)

acceptance_criteria: A kernel test: a signed-in member without content-write invokes redeem from crates/kernel/tests/definitions.rs and the copy is created with the member as creator
A false condition refuses with the condition's error code and commits nothing, and a refused second step commits nothing of the first, each shown by a test
A repeat with the same key and inputs answers the recorded result and changes nothing; with other inputs it is refused with idempotency-mismatch
tasks.description: WG-5045 holds and validates tenant operations (TenantSchema.operations, definitions.rs operation_problems, definer powers in transition.rs require_operation_powers) but nothing invokes one. Where it attaches: an intent variant invoke-operation {operation, inputs, idempotency-key} in specifications/spec.jsonc and a decision in crates/kernel/src/transition.rs: inputs coerced by TenantOperationInput.ty, subject loaded and readable by the invoker, conditions evaluated on the pre-state with params = inputs (D-6548), steps applied in order on the state the earlier steps leave with param.<create step id> bound to the created record, records created with the invoker as creator, workflow guards and policies of the object types not re-checked against the invoker (D-6547) while field types, constraints and unique constraints are; needs() must plan the subject and each step's lookups. Posting steps need the ledger engine and are refused until it exists. Run records keyed by operation, invoker and key for seven days (OPR-1544).
tasks.title: Kernel: invoke a tenant operation (decide-tenant-operation, CT-806)

acceptance_criteria: A kernel test: an automation whose post-ledger step names a unit the catalogue does not declare is refused when it is defined
Removing a ledger unit that a tenant operation posts to is refused while the operation names it, shown by a test
The executable spec functions trigger-def-problems, automation-step-problems and operation-step-problems check the same references with examples
tasks.description: crates/kernel/src/definitions.rs checks every reference a definition makes to the tenant schema (object types, fields, roles, policies, automations, workflow transitions) but not those to the tenant catalogue, which the kernel does not hold: TriggerEvent segment-entered/segment-exited (segment-id), ledger-posted (ledger-unit), setting-changed (setting-id), schedule-due (schedule-id); AutomationStep post-ledger unit, send-mail/create-notice template, call-webhook subscription, fan-out segment; TenantOperationStep post-ledger unit and pool (OPR-1549, OPR-1551). The catalogue is tenant-catalogue, held beside the schema (D-6581, WG-5034). Once the kernel holds it, extend trigger_problems, action_problems and operation_problems to refuse an unknown entry, and refuse a catalogue change that removes an entry a definition names.
tasks.title: Kernel: check catalogue references of triggers, automations and operations (segments, units, pools, templates, settings, schedules)

acceptance_criteria: The spec functions may-confer and require-conferrable give the same check detail as rules.rs may_confer for a role whose powers come from policies, shown by examples
crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs draws an automation whose run-as is writer and still agrees
tasks.description: crates/kernel/src/rules.rs may_confer counts the powers a role grants through policies (missing_policy_powers, holds_policy_power) as well as through role permissions; the spec function may-confer in specifications/spec.jsonc reads role permissions only. So for the owner assigning writer in the notes corpus, the hand kernel writes 'holds every permission that role writer grants' and the generated one 'role writer grants no permission', a difference crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs meets on AssignRole. WG-5045 drew automations with an empty run-as in that test to avoid adding a second case of the same difference.
tasks.title: Spec: may-confer counts the policies of a role as rules.rs may_confer does

acceptance_criteria: A bundle with a trigger, an automation and an operation in the authoring syntax installs through install_into and the tenant schema holds all three
A bundle whose automation names an unknown step is refused at install with the kernel's problem text, shown by a test in crates/substrate
tasks.description: D-6580 gives a tenant bundle sections triggers, automations and operations (values of trigger-def, automation-def and tenant-operation-def). WG-5045 added the schema changes define-trigger, define-automation and define-operation, and the bundle reader crates/substrate/src/bundle.rs now reads composite unique constraints (ObjectSpec.unique) but not those three sections. Expressions in a bundle are written in the authoring syntax (crates/substrate/src/bundle.rs parses text with strata_kernel::expr::parse), while the kernel holds them as the AST type expr, so the reader must parse each expression field of a trigger, an automation step and an operation condition and step.
tasks.title: Bundles: install triggers, automations and operations sections as schema changes

acceptance_criteria: A named query with an equality or range filter on an indexed field and a limit of 20 over 100,000 records loads a number of records bounded by a constant; test for SQLite and the memory store
A query ordered by an indexed field pages by cursor without loading the table; test
A view over a large type loads only the pages its sections show; test
Readers still see only records they may read and results equal the full-scan results on a property test
tasks.description: After WG-5025 only an unfiltered query ordered by id loads a bounded window (Need::PageOf). Every filtered or sorted named query still loads up to 10,001 records and is refused above 10,000 (crates/kernel/src/read.rs), and the view path loads AllOf for every object type a view depends on (crates/backend/src/ops.rs about 326). record_index in crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs indexes field values but reads do not use it.
tasks.title: Push query filters and sort orders into storage, and stop views loading whole tables

acceptance_criteria: POST /internal/lab/apply with a stale revision answers 409 naming the current revision and changes nothing; at the current revision it commits the change once
a test in crates/backend/tests/lab_revision.rs covers the stale and the current case
tasks.description: The Impact Lab only projects; no backend route applies a ChangeSchema from a projection (crates/backend/src/lab.rs, crates/backend/src/http.rs). The kernel's ChangeSchema expected_version (crates/kernel/src/transition.rs change_schema) compares the SCHEMA version, not the state revision, so a schema-version check does not prove the tenant is still at the projected revision. Add an apply route taking the projected revision, refusing with a conflict naming the current revision unless the tenant is still at it, and committing ChangeSchema with expected_version set to the projected schema version.
tasks.title: Lab apply route that checks the revision a projection was taken at

acceptance_criteria: After erase-subject, reading an event stored before the erasure returns no personal value of the subject (test in crates/backend/tests/erasure.rs)
The events_hash and delta_hash of journal entries still verify after the erasure
tasks.description: crates/kernel/src/erasure.rs erases the personal fields of records and emits events without them, but events committed earlier (table events in crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs, DomainEvent bodies record-created, record-updated, record-deleted) keep the full record images for good (tbl-events). PRV-359, PRV-360 and D-350 design a per-subject key whose destruction makes sealed fields unreadable; the key service is not built. Needed: seal personal fields in event bodies under the subject key, or rewrite the stored images at erasure while the sequence and the event hashes stay verifiable.
tasks.title: Erasure: events and the outbox keep the before and after images of erased records

acceptance_criteria: A journal entry written before the erasure holds no personal value of the subject afterwards
Replay of the journal (Impact Lab, crates/simulation) still reaches the same state hash or reports the redaction explicitly
tasks.description: The journal (table journal, JournalEntry in crates/storage-api/src/lib.rs) keeps every intent (create-record and update-record carry field values) and the context (the principal) for good (tbl-journal). Erasure (crates/backend/src/erasure.rs) cannot reach it without the sealed-field design of D-350 and PRV-358 or a replay-safe redaction.
tasks.title: Erasure: journal entries keep the intents and contexts that created the erased values

acceptance_criteria: After erase-subject, no snapshot of the tenant holds a personal value of the subject, or the restore of an older snapshot applies the erasure again
A test restores a snapshot taken before the erasure and finds the subject erased
tasks.description: Table snapshots (create_snapshot in crates/storage-api/src/lib.rs, tbl-snapshots) holds a complete TenantState with every record and the schema with its invitations. Erase-subject does not reach it, and a restore of an older snapshot would bring the erased data back.
tasks.title: Erasure: snapshots of the tenant state keep the personal values

acceptance_criteria: Backups and exports expose no personal value of an erased subject, by key destruction or by an expiry that the receipt states
The erasure receipt names each backup image and export with its expiry
tasks.description: The spec records copy-tenant-backup and copy-tenant-export hold tenant state copies that erase-subject does not reach; D-350 reaches them by destroying the subject key, which is not built (key-service, PRV-358).
tasks.title: Erasure: backups and exports of the tenant keep the personal values

acceptance_criteria: Audit entries that name the subject hold only a sealed form that is destroyed with the subject key
The audit chain verifies before and after an erasure (PRV-359)
tasks.description: Table audit_log (AuditEntry.data, tbl-audit-log) is append-only and keeps events such as sign-ins, SCIM deletes and decisions that can name the principal or a login. Erase-subject cannot rewrite entries (PRV-359), so the entries must be sealed under the subject key (PRV-358, PRV-360, D-350), which is not built.
tasks.title: Erasure: the audit log keeps identifiers and addresses of the subject

acceptance_criteria: No row of schema_history holds an invitation address or a team membership of an erased subject
A backend test lists schema_history after an erasure
tasks.description: Table schema_history (crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs) keeps one schema per version; it may hold invitation addresses and team memberships from before an erasure, and erase-subject rewrites only the current schema (crates/kernel/src/erasure.rs).
tasks.title: Erasure: schema history keeps older invitations and teams of the subject

acceptance_criteria: A personal field with searchable false has no record_index row (test in crates/storage-sqlite)
A searchable personal field is indexed and its row is removed by erase-subject
tasks.description: index_rows in crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs indexes every field value of a record, personal fields included, although D-6585 and PRV-1588 let the index hold a personal field only when its declaration says searchable. Erasure removes the entries when the record is rewritten, but until then the index holds them. The index writer needs the schema (Store::commit has the state) or a filter.
tasks.title: Record index writes personal values whether or not the field is searchable

acceptance_criteria: restrict-subject stores a restriction and every read that names the personal fields of the subject is refused (PRV-352)
Erasure of a restricted subject follows the rule PRV-352 states, tested in crates/backend/tests/erasure.rs
tasks.description: No store of restrictions exists (rec-restriction is target) and the contract restrict-subject (CT-212) has no code. Erasure (crates/kernel/src/erasure.rs, crates/backend/src/erasure.rs) states in its receipt that restrictions are not built.
tasks.title: Restrictions of processing (PRV-352) are not built, so erasure cannot report them

acceptance_criteria: place-legal-hold stores a hold and erase-subject leaves each held record unchanged and reports it
The erase-subject receipt lists the held records
tasks.description: rec-legal-hold and the contract place-legal-hold (CT-215) have no code. The contract erase-subject lists a conflict error for a hold and nothing returns it. Erasure must leave each record a hold names unchanged and report it.
tasks.title: Legal holds (PRV-355) are not built, so a hold cannot suspend an erasure

acceptance_criteria: export-subject-data returns every declared personal field of every record whose subject is the principal, with the membership and the teams of the principal
A principal of another tenant, and another subject, are not in the export (test)
tasks.description: Export needs the enumeration of erasure (crates/kernel/src/erasure.rs: declared fields, by-field lookups and creator scans) read-only, plus the account, the memberships and the identity documents of the principal. Not built in the erasure slice.
tasks.title: Subject export (export-subject-data, CT-210) is not built

acceptance_criteria: A record whose retention period has ended and that nothing refers to is deleted by the erasure of its subject
A field declared to name its subject by a reference to a person record is resolved through a stated principal-to-record mapping, or refused at declaration
tasks.description: crates/kernel/src/erasure.rs clears personal fields and never deletes a record, and it cannot match a subject field typed as a reference to the record of a person (it reports it in not-erased). PRV-357 deletes records whose retention has ended with the reach of an erasure; the retention job is not built.
tasks.title: Erasure: delete records whose retention has ended, and resolve subject fields that reference a person record

acceptance_criteria: After erase-subject, an invitation addressed to the verified address of the subject cannot be redeemed
The journal and the events carry no address (test)
tasks.description: The kernel holds no address of a person, so crates/kernel/src/erasure.rs revokes only invitations the subject issued and clears the address of those the subject redeemed. An invitation addressed to the subject that nobody redeemed stays pending. The backend knows the verified address (Store::verified_address) before it removes the account.
tasks.title: Erasure: invitations addressed to the subject but not yet redeemed are not reached

acceptance_criteria: Erasing a subject removes the stored bytes of each file referred to only by personal fields of the subject
The receipt names each file removed
tasks.description: PRV-1586 and D-6585 ask erasure to remove the files a personal file field refers to. The kernel clears the field value; no file store call removes the bytes (rec-file-bytes).
tasks.title: Erasure: files and file bytes of personal file fields are not reached

acceptance_criteria: A spec whose shipped record lacks the statement fails exegra validate with a code naming the record
A negative fixture of the rule exists in the Exegra tests
tasks.description: Exegra should refuse a spec in which a shipped record of scope tenant-meta or platform that can name a principal carries an erasure text that does not state whether the erasure of a subject (contract erase-subject) reaches it. Found while building erase-subject: events, journal, snapshots, audit log and schema history all keep copies that their erasure texts did not mention.
tasks.title: Exegra: a shipped table or copy that can hold personal data must say how erase-subject treats it

acceptance_criteria: Exegra validate of a project whose products list Strata's promotions.jsonc reports errors 0
Each of the nine operators has a passing and a type-mismatch case in tests/core/layer-expr.test.js, with the same rule codes specc gives
A test fails if the language entity gains an operator that layer-expr.js does not handle
tasks.description: src/core/layer-expr.js (from branch wg5060) parses and checks expressions in product files with its own parser of the tenant rule language. Branch wgops added nine operators to the language (checked add, subtract, multiply; timestamp plus and minus milliseconds; ms_between; days, hours, minutes; concat; text) in src/core/language.js and language-eval.js. The two were written in parallel, so layer-expr.js has none of the operators: a product file that uses them (Strata's crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/promotions.jsonc does) is refused with layer.expr-syntax. Strata's specc has the same gap in crates/spec-compiler/src/layer_expr.rs and is being fixed there; the two must agree on syntax, typing and error codes.
tasks.title: Exegra: the product-expression checker does not know the rule-language arithmetic and time operators

acceptance_criteria: A kernel function maps a tenant schema and a principal to an audience class, equal for two principals exactly when no Read policy or field read rule of the schema tells them apart, with a test where a policy reads the principal and gives each principal its own class

An aggregate result is stored under a key containing the class and the revision of each object type it depends on, a commit to that object type makes a new key, and a result stored for one class is never served to a principal of another (tests in crates/kernel/tests and crates/backend/tests/aggregates.rs)
tasks.description: The kernel does not compute an audience class today (grep audience in crates/kernel finds nothing), so crates/kernel/src/aggregates.rs run() computes for the asking principal every time and crates/backend/src/aggregates.rs stores and shares nothing. CPY-005, AGG-033, D-15 and D-5065 need the kernel to derive, from the tenant's policies, which principals are indistinguishable for a read, and AGG-030 to AGG-034 need the copy keyed by tenant, query, aggregate, arguments, class, schema version and object-type revisions (D-5064). Add the derivation in a new kernel module, tag AggregateResult consumers with the class, and add the copy-store entry; the contract postcondition on a stored copy in specifications aggregate-run is disclaimed in its description until then.
tasks.title: Kernel derives audience classes; aggregate results are keyed and stored per class

acceptance_criteria: The 121st anonymous GET /api/aggregate from one source address within a minute is answered 429 with a retry-after header; the 120th is not
Requests to /api/view and to pages are not counted against the aggregate rate, and the aggregate rate is not counted against theirs (test in crates/bff)
tasks.description: The specification states 120 anonymous calls a minute per source address for aggregate-run (quota q-aggregate-run, throttled error). The BFF route GET /api/aggregate (crates/bff/src/routes.rs aggregate_run) is not counted: is_page_or_view in routes.rs counts only /api/view and pages, against the 600 a minute admission rate in crates/bff/src/limits.rs. Add a rate of its own for the aggregate route with the stated limit and a throttled reply naming the limit and the time after which the next request is permitted (CMS-168).
tasks.title: Per-source quota q-aggregate-run on GET /api/aggregate

acceptance_criteria: Spec functions state the problems of aggregates and declared fields and the aggregate computation, each with examples taken from the hand-computed cases of crates/kernel/tests/aggregates.rs
The generated_differential test draws schemas with aggregates and sections that name one and compares the hand-written and generated results with no difference 11 guard left
tasks.description: crates/kernel/src/aggregates.rs is hand-written only. The generated schema-problems, section-problems, view-problems, view-read and assemble-view of specifications/spec.jsonc state nothing about aggregates, declared-fields or a view section naming an aggregate, and no spec function states the aggregate itself (aggregate-request is a type of its own because a variant of read-request would break the exhaustive matches of read-needs and kernel-read). crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs lists this as difference 11 with a guard. Add spec functions with examples for the definition-time problems, the aggregate computation and the view section, then remove difference 11 and its guard.
tasks.title: Mirror aggregates in the specification functions and the differential

acceptance_criteria: A bundle with a query that declares an aggregate and a view section that names it installs, and the aggregate answers through /internal/aggregate (test in crates/backend/tests/aggregates.rs)
A bundle whose aggregate names a field the query does not declare is refused at install with the kernel's problem text
tasks.description: crates/substrate/src/bundle.rs builds each QueryDef with aggregates: None and declared_fields: None and each ViewSection with aggregate: None, so a bundle (tenants/*/tenant.json and templates) cannot declare an aggregate or a view section that names one; they can only be declared by a ChangeSchema intent. Add the bundle fields (query aggregates and declared fields, section aggregate), the tenant-bundle type and the loader checks, and give the publication template one leaderboard-style aggregate as an example.
tasks.title: Tenant bundles declare aggregates and declared fields

acceptance_criteria: The route refuses a tenant that is not the one resolved from the host and session with tenant-mismatch, is recorded as an audit entry, and contract aggregate-run-signed-in is shipped with bffRoute
A test where a Read policy of the object type follows a reference into another object type shows that type in depends_on, and a test without one still shows the object type alone
tasks.description: GET /api/aggregate serves signed-in callers by session already, but contract aggregate-run-signed-in (CT-311) is still deployment target: it takes a tenant input and answers tenant-mismatch, which the route does not do. Separately, AggregateResult.depends_on (crates/kernel/src/aggregates.rs depends_on) names the query's object type and the types followed by the query filter and by the read rules of the fields named, but not the types that the Read policies of the object type follow (AGG-042), so a change to such a type does not change an aggregate key.
tasks.title: aggregate-run-signed-in (CT-311) and depends-on through Read policies

acceptance_criteria: Exegra validate refuses, with a negative fixture, a scenario-run machine with storage.creates true, no instances.key and a key field whose type is not string, uuid, an integer or an id or scalar over one; the Strata spec still validates with errors 0
Exegra validate refuses, with a negative fixture, two such machines in one record whose integer keys would both be 0

Exegra validate refuses, with a negative fixture, a retry-event whose attempts is 10 or more on an event of an implementation-level machine, and docs/semantics.md states the singleton rule and the attempt cap
tasks.description: WG-5090 and WG-5074 were closed on the Strata side (branch w3rt) by a runtime rule Exegra does not yet check. (1) An implementation-level machine with storage.creates true and no instances.key is one instance that the runtime creates when the system host is built, under a key specc derives from the machine id (crates/spec-compiler/src/backend/machines.rs singleton_key_json; decision D-7440): string key = machine id with - written _, uuid key = a version 8 uuid from the machine id, integer key = 0, composite = array. A key field of any other type (enum, struct, bytes, optional, f64) has no such key and specc refuses it (specc.singleton-key); Exegra should refuse it first, as a rule in src/core/readiness-machines.js beside machine.initial-unreachable. Two such machines that share a record and have an integer key collide on key 0; refuse that too. docs/semantics.md (the paragraph on machine.initial-unreachable, line 152) should state the singleton rule. (2) The runtime dispatches an at-least-once message at most 10 times (RetryPolicy::max_attempts, D-7441) and then dead-letters it, so a retry-event fault with attempts of 10 or more is not realisable: fault.unrealisable (src/core/fault-model.js faultRealisability) should refuse it, and strata_spec_compiler::scenarios::unrealisable mirrors it. Exegra is off limits to the Strata agent; this is for its owner.
tasks.title: Exegra: refuse an unkeyed creating machine whose key the runtime cannot fill, and a retry-event beyond the runtime's attempt cap

acceptance_criteria: Exegra validate of a spec that uses gotoPath with fragment, captureMail and expectUrl reports no uiScenario.step error, and a fixture with a fragment holding a space, '#', '/' or '?' is refused with uiScenario.fragment; a captureMail without 'to', 'pattern' or 'name', and an expectUrl without 'pattern', are refused
applying C:/dev/audit-wave/ops/w3e2e-exegra.ops.json after the w3e2e operations validates with errors 0 and warnings 0 against C:/dev/strata-w3e2e/specifications/spec.jsonc
tasks.description: specc (crates/spec-compiler/src/e2e.rs, branch w3e2e) now lowers three additions that Exegra's own step table (src/core/ui-steps.js STEP_KINDS and checkJourney) refuses. Exactly: (1) gotoPath gains key 'fragment': a string that, once ${name} references are replaced by 'x', is non-empty and matches /^[A-Za-z0-9=&_.~%-]+$/ (code uiScenario.fragment); a ${name} in it must be a captured value. (2) new step captureMail with keys to, pattern, name, as, timeoutMs: 'to' and 'pattern' non-empty strings, 'pattern' compiles as a regular expression (as the other pattern keys do), 'name' is defined like capture's name (duplicate is uiScenario.capture-duplicate), 'as' if present is one of the journey's browsers, timeoutMs a positive integer. (3) new step expectUrl with keys pattern, absent, timeoutMs: pattern a non-empty regular expression, absent a boolean. Update the Exegra spec first (specs/exegra/spec.jsonc, per its AGENTS.md), then src/core/ui-steps.js, tests, docs/model-and-format.md. After it lands, apply C:/dev/audit-wave/ops/w3e2e-exegra.ops.json (three uiScenarios ui-accept-invitation, ui-emailed-link-sign-in, ui-sign-in-pages-accessible and the steps of five federation journeys) to the Strata spec. Sources: WG-5071.
tasks.title: Exegra: accept gotoPath fragment, captureMail and expectUrl in user journeys

acceptance_criteria: specc lowers apiCall with form and expectHeaders and refuses a call with both body and form; tests in crates/spec-compiler/tests/e2e.rs and the unit tests of e2e.rs cover both
tests/e2e/step-fixtures/spec.jsonc has pass- and violates- journeys for both keys and a uiScenario ui-service-account-token verifies tok-001 and tok-009 on the Strata spec
tasks.description: Hand-written tests in tests/e2e/site.spec.js cannot become spec journeys because apiCall (crates/spec-compiler/src/e2e.rs lower_api_call; Exegra src/core/ui-steps.js apiCall) has only a JSON body and reads no response header: 'a service account is made on the desk side, gets a token, and rotating its secret ends the old one' (line 1622) posts application/x-www-form-urlencoded to /token and /introspect and reads the cache-control header; 'ten wrong passwords lock a login' (line 1051) asserts the reply carries no set-cookie; the SAML metadata test (line 1602) asserts content-type. Add to apiCall a 'form' key (object of strings, sent form-encoded, exclusive with 'body') and 'expectHeaders' (object of header name to expected string, or null for absent), in specc and Exegra, each with a passing and a failing fixture in tests/e2e/step-fixtures/spec.jsonc and server.mjs, then write the journeys ui-service-account-token and extend ui-saml-metadata and ui-login-lockout.
tasks.title: Journey steps: form-encoded apiCall bodies and response header assertions

acceptance_criteria: specc lowers fillLabel (or the chosen name), forward and dropConnection with unit tests in e2e.rs and a passing and a failing fixture each in tests/e2e/step-fixtures/spec.jsonc
journeys ui-step-up-with-password and an extension of ui-revoked-session... (ui-sessions-list-and-revoke) that drops the revoked browser's connection before the revocation exist in the Strata spec
tasks.description: Three gaps found moving tests/e2e/site.spec.js into journeys. (1) A password input has no WAI-ARIA role, so a journey cannot type into the step-up confirmation (alertdialog 'Confirm that it is you', test at line 1471) or the sign-in password except through a spec form field: add a fill form that names a control by accessible label within an element ({label, within, value}). (2) No forward step (test 'a delete confirmation does not survive leaving the desk and coming back', line 349, uses goBack then goForward). (3) The page's own test hook window.__strataDropSocket (web/src) cannot be called, so IDN-013's 'including when the revocation notice is lost' and the reconnect journey's 'waiting' state cannot be shown: add a dropConnection step that closes the live connection of the current browser. Specc side in crates/spec-compiler/src/e2e.rs with pass and violates fixtures in tests/e2e/step-fixtures; Exegra's step table needs the same additions.
tasks.title: Journey steps: fill a control by label, forward, and dropping the live connection

acceptance_criteria: a function body with eval(tenant-rule-language, e, env, lookup) compiles, and its generated Rust gives the same answer as Exegra for an example whose condition follows a reference (present, absent, and not covered)

tasks.description: Exegra evaluates eval(L, e, env, lookup) where lookup is map<string, map<string, map<string, V>>> (docs/model-and-format.md, Functions; src/core/language-eval.js, 'through': lookup[field][target id as text][attribute]; a missing lookup is the error '<field> cannot be followed here', a field the lookup does not cover is 'the lookup does not cover <field>', a covered target that is absent gives null). specc refuses it: crates/spec-compiler/src/function/typing.rs ("eval" | "check" => arity(3, op)) accepts three arguments only, function/rust.rs emits support::<bridge>(e, env), and crates/spec-compiler/src/language.rs Bridge writes a follow() that always returns 'following a reference needs a lookup, and none is available'. This is why the spec functions authorize, kernel-read's filters and redact cannot follow a reference (difference 2 of crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs, WG-5096, WG-4938, WG-4957). Accept a fourth argument of that type, pass it to a bridge whose follow() reads it as language-eval.js does, and give the bridge for three arguments its present behaviour.
tasks.title: specc: compile eval of a language with a lookup (the fourth argument) in function bodies

acceptance_criteria: utf8Length('a') is 1, utf8Length of a two-byte character 2, of a three-byte 3, of a four-byte 4, in an Exegra example

tasks.description: The function language has length(s) (characters) and no way to measure the UTF-8 encoding of a string, which limits.rs counts (str::len: MAX_STRING_BYTES 65536, the encoded size of a unique value 200 bytes, a record of 262144 bytes of JSON). The spec states them through utf8-length (specifications/spec.jsonc, WG-5092), which compares every character with three bounds through sortBy: it is exact (examples with two, three and four byte characters) but allocates per character on a path every record write takes. Add the operation utf8Length(s) (u64: Rust s.len()) to src/core/function.js and function-syntax.js, type it, document it in docs/model-and-format.md, and tell specc (crates/spec-compiler/src/function) to compile it to s.len(). Then utf8-char-len, utf8-length and string-at-least can be deleted.
tasks.title: Exegra: a byte-length operation for strings

tasks.description: kernel-cases.json (Exegra tests/fixtures/language/kernel-cases.json and its byte-identical copy crates/spec-compiler-language-fixture/tests/kernel-cases.json) holds parse, print, eval and check cases whose sources all parse. The parsers are therefore not held to each other on what they refuse or on the text of the refusal. WG-5089 gave the language a JavaScript parser (tenant-rule-language.js) and chose to differ from the Rust parser in one place: a number literal beyond +-(2^53-1) is refused by the JavaScript parser at parse time with 'number out of range: <digits>', where the Rust parser accepts up to the 64-bit range (Token::Int(i64)); and its refusal texts for exotic characters follow Rust's Debug only for ASCII. Needed in Exegra: a 'parse' section of cases (source, result Ok with the expression or Err with the exact text) covering an unterminated string, a bad escape, an unexpected character, an unknown name, a trailing token, an argument list of the wrong length, a role id that breaks its constraints, a negative record id and a literal at +-(2^53-1) and one past it; and the decision whether the Rust parser should also refuse beyond +-(2^53-1) so the two agree on acceptance.
tasks.title: Add parse-refusal cases to the shared tenant rule language case table, so the Rust, JavaScript and Exegra parsers are held to one set of refusals

tasks.description: D-6548 and OPR-1544 keep a run record of each accepted invocation for seven days keyed by operation, invoker and idempotency key (record rec-tenant-operation-run, realisation target). WG-5100 (commit 1932c5d, slice w3ops) uses the store idempotency instead: strata_storage_api::execute_by with Context.idempotency_key, kept IDEMPOTENCY_RETENTION_MS = 24 h and scoped by tenant and principal only, so (a) a repeat between 24 h and 7 days is decided again (postings are still protected by their ledger keys, OPR-1545), (b) the same key on two different operations by one person is a mismatch rather than two runs, (c) the mismatch reaches the backend as ErrorKind::InvalidIntent and crates/backend/src/operations.rs explain() re-reads the store to answer 409 IdempotencyMismatch. Closing it needs the run record in the Store trait (crates/storage-api/src/lib.rs), memory.rs, storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs and conformance.rs, or a per-entry retention on IdempotencyEntry, plus an error kind for idempotency-mismatch (error-kind in the spec, CT-806 errors).

Wiring, as the doc comment on post_to_ledger states: call crate::ledger::post(&State{tenant_id, tenant: Some(Arc::new(self.work.clone())), coverage: self.coverage.clone()}, &request, self.ctx, self.ctx.now); on acceptance append its delta ops to self.ops and apply them to self.work so a later step sees the balance, append its events, push LedgerPostingResult.entry to self.entries; return a refusal (below-floor, above-cap, above-period-cap, unknown-unit) as it is; make the method take &mut self. Add the posting needs (account, balance, limits, entry of the key) to plan() in the same file.
tasks.title: Wire tenant-operation posting steps to the ledger engine

tasks.description: run_step in crates/backend/src/worker/steps.rs fails the run when a step spends its attempts but does not run the compensate steps (AutomationStepDef.compensate) of the completed steps in reverse order (SCH-1525, workflow-compensation-flow). Attach in its failure branch: set the run compensating and create a job for the compensation of the last completed step; StepState needs a compensated value.
tasks.title: Automation worker: compensation of completed steps (SCH-1525, WFL-005)

acceptance_criteria: A test: two events with one run key start one run and write one declined record with reason run-key-repeated
A test: runs of one key start in event-sequence order and none while an earlier one is open

Needs a run-key store (rec-automation-run-key) holding the hash of every key a run started for while the automation exists, a declined exception record with reason run-key-repeated for a repeat (D-6534), and starts per trigger and key in event-sequence order with one open run per key (D-6532).
tasks.title: Automation worker: run keys and ordering by run key (SCH-1534, SCH-1536)

acceptance_criteria: A conformance check: an ended job older than thirty days is removed by the purge and a younger one is kept
An unsettled dead-lettered exception record is never purged, shown by a test
tasks.description: The tables jobs, automation_runs, automation_steps and automation_exceptions (crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs tenant migration 12; crates/storage-api/src/memory.rs) are never purged. rec-job keeps thirty days after the outcome, rec-workflow-run and rec-workflow-step-run ninety days after the run ends, rec-automation-exception ninety days for declined and held and until settled for parked and dead-lettered (OPS-348). Add a Store purge operation, call it from purge() in crates/backend/src/lib.rs, and tighten ret-tbl-jobs and the other retentions in the spec.

Add routes in crates/backend/src/worker/routes.rs (list-jobs needs jobs-read; cancel-job and retry-job need jobs-manage and record the requester and reason, AGT-416 to AGT-418), bffRoute for the public ones, and mark them shipped.
tasks.title: Automation worker: serve schedule-job, lease-job, report-job-result, list-jobs, cancel-job and retry-job

acceptance_criteria: validate stays at errors 0 with automation-worker at a status other than not-implemented
Each of the eight machines is either run by the backend or declared target

Decide: run those machines through strata-runtime as crates/backend/src/outbox.rs does, or declare them target and the worker hand-written; then set the status and move the contracts back.

acceptance_criteria: Creating an account or a SCIM user with principal id automation:x is refused, shown by a backend test
No seeded principal id starts with automation:, checked by a test over tenants/
tasks.description: The kernel refuses the prefix automation: for owners, role assignments, team members and callers with a session (reserved_problem in crates/kernel/src/automation.rs), but the shell mints principal ids for accounts, invitations, SCIM users and federated identities without checking it (crates/backend/src/signin, crates/backend/src/service/scim.rs, crates/backend/src/provision.rs). Refuse such ids where they are minted.
tasks.title: Identity: refuse principal ids that start with automation:

acceptance_criteria: The spec states the choice in a decision and the code follows it
A test: an automation that runs one step twice applies its effect twice, or the definition is refused
tasks.description: D-6528 derives the step key from the tenant, automation, run, step name and member. step_key in crates/backend/src/worker/steps.rs follows it, so a run that loops back to a step (crates/kernel/src/definitions.rs allows cycles through a branch) reuses the key: the second visit replays the first result or is refused as a reused idempotency key. The owner decides: add the position of the step in the run to the key, or refuse cycles in automation_problems.
tasks.title: Automation step key repeats when a run visits a step twice (D-6528)

acceptance_criteria: A test: a step retried 25 hours after a lost report does not create a second record
The spec states how long a step key is kept
tasks.description: A step's record change is made once through the kernel idempotency record of its step key (crates/backend/src/worker/steps.rs), kept for IDEMPOTENCY_RETENTION_MS, 24 hours (crates/storage-api/src/lib.rs). A step's attempts can span more than a day (ten attempts, delays up to one day, D-6529) and a released dead-lettered step keeps its key (SCH-1524), so a late retry can apply a change twice. Keep step-key records for the life of the run, or check the step record before deciding.
tasks.title: Automation step effects can outlive the 24-hour idempotency retention

acceptance_criteria: A backend or worker test defines a segment over 250 records, changes its predicate, runs the worker, and the membership equals a fresh evaluation with the batch rows gone
A time-dependent indexable segment's person leaves at the first worker refresh after the wake time, and a refresh with no quota records refresh_skipped_at on the segment
A trigger on segment-entered gets a job created from the segment event log, and the log position is marked published
tasks.description: Segments (WG-5082 slice w3seg) leave continuations as rec-segment-batch rows (scopes all, ref:<field>:<record>, due) and write entry/exit events to the segment block's own ordered log (rec-segment-event, d-7280). Nothing runs them yet. The kernel side is crates/kernel/src/segments.rs (batch_load, batch_targets, start_refresh, skip_refresh) and the store side crates/storage-api/src/segments.rs (run_batch, run_pending, start_refresh, skip_refresh, Store::segment_batches, Store::segment_events_after). The worker must: create one job per pending batch and call segments::run_batch in its own transaction (CT-297); run a schedule per time-dependent segment at its refresh_seconds calling segments::start_refresh (SEG-018), or segments::skip_refresh when the daily job quota has no room (SEG-1544); count segment jobs against the admission rate and daily quota (SEG-1543); read segment_events_after as the outbox of entry/exit events and create trigger jobs for triggers on segment-entered/segment-exited (SEG-014), declining past the hop limit (SEG-032); and mark the log published.
tasks.title: Job worker runs segment batches, refreshes and the segment event log

acceptance_criteria: crates/substrate/tests/product_bundle.rs installs a bundle with a segments section, the tenant's segment catalogue holds the segment under the derived id, and InstalledRecord.owns lists it
Installing the same bundle twice gives the same segment-id and version 1; removing the product removes the segment and writes no exit event
tasks.description: WG-5082 asks that install_product accept the segments section. Segments are now kept in a storage block beside the tenant state (crates/kernel/src/segments.rs, crates/storage-api/src/segments.rs, SQLite tenant migration 12), not in the tenant schema, so the install in crates/backend/src/seed.rs / crates/substrate/src/bundle.rs must call strata_storage_api::segments::define with strata_kernel::segments::from_decl(tenant, key, decl, principal_field, visible) after the schema commit, with the segment-id derived by derive_segment_id (D-6582); a removal calls segments::remove for each owned segment. segment-decl gains optional principal-field and visible-to-members (ops file w3seg). UNBUILT_SECTIONS in crates/substrate/src/bundle.rs still names segments.
tasks.title: Install, upgrade and remove the segments section of a product bundle

acceptance_criteria: Restoring a snapshot taken before a membership change leaves, after the batches run, membership equal to a fresh evaluation (test in crates/storage-api conformance or backend tests)
An erasure test removes the person's memberships with sealed exit events and a later change does not re-enter them, through the real erasure path
A subscription with a segments selector receives the entry event of a person whose subject record the subscriber may read, and nothing for one it may not
tasks.description: Three loose ends of the segment block (crates/kernel/src/segments.rs, crates/storage-api/src/segments.rs, crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs migration 12). (1) The erasure transaction of PRV-353 does not exist; when it is built it must call strata_storage_api::segments::erase(store, ctx, person, sealed) with the sealed form of the person (SEG-036 to SEG-038). (2) Store::restore_snapshot in crates/storage-api/src/memory.rs and crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs restores the tenant state but not the segment rows, so membership can disagree with the restored records; restore must re-run every segment as a changed predicate (an all-scope batch per segment) or snapshot the block. (3) crates/substrate/src/subscribe.rs Selector::new still refuses a segments member saying no segment event is emitted; entry/exit events now exist in the segment event log (d-7280) and need a delivery path and a read decision (SEG-033).
tasks.title: Segments: erasure wiring, snapshot restore, and subscription selector

acceptance_criteria: A policy with resource ledger and condition record.owner == principal lets a holder of ledger-read read only their own entries; a kernel test in crates/kernel/tests/ledger.rs shows another person's entries are left out of read_entries and of the balance
read_ranked leaves out an account of which the reader's policies do not permit every entry (LDG-1544), shown by a test
Exegra validate errors 0, warnings 0 with the resource variant added
tasks.description: The kernel ledger (crates/kernel/src/ledger.rs, commit 1c43b08 on branch w3ledger) authorises reads by capability only: ledger-read reads every account, ledger-read-own only the caller's (fn may_read). D-6550 and LDG-1540 add a policy resource 'ledger' (optionally of one unit) whose condition reads owner, pool, unit, scope and, for an entry, amount, reason, caused_by and at; LDG-024, LDG-025 and LDG-1544 then filter entries, balances (derive-ledger-balance, CT-288) and ranked listings by those policies. Not done: the spec union 'resource' has no ledger variant, and rules.rs authorize, schema.rs policy checks and the spec functions request-text, resource-debug, policy-applies and policy-problems would each need an arm.
tasks.title: Ledger: policies over the ledger resource and policy-filtered balances

acceptance_criteria: A debit to an account of a unit with an expiry consumes the oldest bucket first (LDG-1545), shown by a kernel test

expire-ledger-credits posts one entry per account with credit left in an ended bucket, with key expiry:<bucket start>, at most 100 accounts per transaction, and a repeated batch posts nothing twice (LDG-1546, LDG-1547), shown by a test
tasks.description: Expiry of ledger credits is not built. crates/kernel/src/ledger.rs (commit 1c43b08, branch w3ledger) has no buckets: the account header (spec type ledger-account) keeps balance, last-sequence and period totals only, and the spec type ledger-unit-decl, which the schema change declare-ledger-unit carries, has no expiry field (rec-ledger-unit has one; CT-284 takes one). The backend route /internal/ledger/declare-unit (crates/backend/src/ledger.rs) refuses an expiry. Needed: an expiry on the unit declaration, buckets on the header consumed oldest first by debits, and the job expire-ledger-credits (CT-812) posting minus the remainder with key expiry:<bucket start> in batches of 100 accounts through an index of the oldest bucket.
tasks.title: Ledger: credit expiry by period (D-6553, LDG-1545 to LDG-1547)

acceptance_criteria: The generated kernel_transition and the hand-written transition agree on PostLedger and on the ledger schema changes in crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs, with difference 11 and its guard removed
Exegra validate errors 0, warnings 0 and no new gap
tasks.description: Branch w3ledger (commit 1c43b08, operations file C:/dev/audit-wave/ops/w3ledger.ops.json) added need.ledger, delta-op.ledger, intent.post-ledger, four ledger schema changes, tenant-schema.ledger and tenant-state.ledger. The shared spec functions only got placeholder arms so their matches stay exhaustive: intent-decision refuses post-ledger, apply-change refuses the ledger changes, needs plans no ledger need, apply-delta ignores ledger ops, need-order ranks ledger needs last without ordering them among themselves, and the functions that rebuild tenant-schema or tenant-state drop their ledger member. crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs lists this as difference 11 and guards it (assert_no_input_of_a_known_difference). Write spec functions mirroring crates/kernel/src/ledger.rs (decide-ledger-posting and friends, with examples), wire them into those arms, carry ledger: schema.ledger / ledger: s.ledger in every construction, and let the differential draw ledger declarations and postings.
tasks.title: Mirror the tenant ledger in the spec functions and remove difference 11

acceptance_criteria: An erasure request for a principal who owns an account and caused entries leaves the account without an owner and the entries without caused_by, with every balance unchanged, shown by a backend or runtime test
The erasure receipt lists the number of ledger accounts and entries cleared
tasks.description: Branch w3ledger (commit 1c43b08) adds Store::anonymise_ledger_principal (crates/storage-api/src/lib.rs; memory store in crates/storage-api/src/memory.rs, SQLite in crates/storage-sqlite/src/ledger.rs fn anonymise), which clears a principal from the accounts it owns and from caused_by of the entries it caused and keeps every amount and balance (LDG-027, LDG-028, retentions ret-ledger-account and ret-ledger-entry). Nothing calls it yet: the erasure of a principal (the subject-erasure work of slice w3erase) must call it in the same request, and the receipt must count what it cleared. D-5012 also seals those fields under the principal's key until cleared (PRV-358), which is not built.
tasks.title: Erasure clears the principal from the ledger (call Store::anonymise_ledger_principal)

acceptance_criteria: A tenant with 10,000 account limits decides a posting without loading the limits of other accounts, shown by a kernel test that counts the needs
A runtime or backend entry point answers CT-287 with ok, stored and replayed for one account, and reports a gap in the numbers
A subscriber selecting units receives a notice for a posting of that unit and nothing that names the owner to anyone else

(1) Account limits live in tenant-schema.ledger.limits (crates/kernel/src/ledger.rs), so up to 10,000 of them (LDG-1550) load with every schema; D-6554 calls an account limit one record per exception, best loaded by need with its account header. (2) verify-ledger-balance (CT-287) is not served: ledger::replayed_balance exists but no runtime job compares stored balances with the journal. (3) crates/substrate/src/subscribe.rs gives ledger-entry-posted no notice and Selector::new still refuses units (SCH-1575), so a subscriber cannot hear postings of a unit.
tasks.title: Ledger: account limits out of the tenant schema, verify-ledger-balance, and socket notices for postings

Exegra refuses crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/refused/query-value-invalid.jsonc, view-value-invalid.jsonc, workflow-value-invalid.jsonc with layer.value-invalid and view-query-unknown.jsonc with layer.reference-unknown, and accepts crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/bundle/ticket-board.jsonc

Exegra layer-values.js (C:/dev/exegra/src/core/layer-values.js) needs the same rows in the same order: [objects, policies, queries, views, workflows, segments, settings, ledgerUnits, ...] with entries [section, type, idField]: [queries, query-def, id], [views, view-def, id], [workflows, workflow-def, id]. layer-expr.js needs the scope rows: queries = fields of the object type named by item.object and the params listed in item.params; workflows = fields of item.object and no params. The test exegra_lists_the_same_typed_sections in crates/spec-compiler/tests/layers.rs compares the two tables and fails until this lands, and exegra_refuses_each_refused_product_with_the_same_rule fails for the refused fixtures query-value-invalid, view-value-invalid, workflow-value-invalid and view-query-unknown.

acceptance_criteria: Exegra accepts crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/badge-milestones.jsonc and promotions.jsonc with version and platform in the header
Exegra refuses header-version-invalid.jsonc and header-platform-invalid.jsonc with layer.header-invalid, and has a negative fixture of its own for each of the three malformed cases
tasks.description: specc layers.rs (crates/spec-compiler/src/layers.rs check_header, WG-5080) now accepts the header keys version and platform and validates them: version is three whole numbers joined by dots (is_version); platform is an object with min (a platform release: one to three whole numbers, optionally a hyphen and a label) and optionally below (a release later than min, numbers compared without trailing zeros), no other key; a malformed one is layer.header-invalid, the messages are in platform_problems. Exegra layers.js (C:/dev/exegra/src/core/layers.js) refuses any header key but id, name, description and imports. It must take version and platform with the same validation and the same rule code, and its fixtures (tests/fixtures/layers/refused of Exegra) need a negative one each: a version 1.0, a platform with no min, and a platform whose below is not later than min. The specc fixtures are crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/refused/header-version-invalid.jsonc and header-platform-invalid.jsonc, and the fixtures badge-milestones.jsonc and promotions.jsonc now carry version and platform in their headers, so Exegra refuses them until it takes the keys.
tasks.title: Exegra: accept product.version and product.platform in the product header

acceptance_criteria: install_product installs the ledger-units section of crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/expected/badge-milestones.bundle.json without removing it by hand, and the removal of the product removes the unit
no section of bundle-sections is refused by name any more: UNBUILT_SECTIONS in crates/substrate/src/product.rs is empty and the six refuse_ functions are gone
tasks.description: crates/substrate/src/product.rs refuses these sections by name through six functions, each called once in ProductBundle::from_json: refuse_capabilities, refuse_segments, refuse_settings, refuse_ledger_units, refuse_ledger_pools, refuse_ledger_limits. When the kernel holds a section (kernel/src/segments.rs, settings.rs, ledger.rs and the capability change of the settings module, built by other agents), the change for that section is: in the kernel nothing but the schema change that defines it; in the substrate, replace the call of its refuse_ function by a reader (parse_list over the section, key by the id member, convert expressions with expressions_of_*), add the map to ProductBundle, add its kind to ProductBundle::entities, definition_changes, same_in, removal_change and removal_rank, and drop the section from UNBUILT_SECTIONS and add it to BUILT_SECTIONS. The tests each_section_without_a_kernel_intent_is_refused_naming_it and the_bundles_specc_writes_are_read_and_their_unbuilt_sections_are_named in crates/substrate/tests/product_bundle.rs lose the section they cover; badge-milestones installs with its ledger-units then (crates/backend/tests/products.rs removes ledger-units by hand).
tasks.title: Installer takes the sections capabilities, segments, settings and ledger declarations of a bundle

acceptance_criteria: a ChangeSchema that defines a field on an object type a product owns is refused with a message naming the entity and the product, and the same change inside the install, upgrade or removal of that product is accepted (test in crates/kernel/tests/object_meta.rs)
the generated functions are not changed without a known-difference entry in crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs
tasks.description: D-6582 and INT-1582: a change from outside the product to an entity it owns is refused; the owner changes it by an upgrade. The kernel holds the ownership record now (crates/kernel/src/products.rs, tenant-schema.products) but change_schema in crates/kernel/src/transition.rs does not look at it: any owner schema change may redefine or remove an entity a product owns, and the next upgrade then computes its difference from a record that no longer matches. The rule: a ChangeSchema whose changes touch an entity (an object type and its fields and constraints, a role, a policy, a workflow, a query, a view, a template, a token, a trigger, an automation, an operation) that products::owner_of names is refused unless the same change carries record-product or remove-product for that product. Add the function to products.rs (changes -> the owned entities they touch), one call in change_schema after require_definition_authority, and a refusal text that names the entity and the product.
tasks.title: Refuse a schema change from outside a product to an entity the product owns

acceptance_criteria: the specification has a type for a block and a statement of how a block names a token, and crates/kernel/src/templates.rs refuses a template that names an undefined token and a token that refers to itself, with tests in crates/kernel/tests/object_meta.rs
the fixtures of the products under crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products use blocks of that schema
tasks.description: The specification says only that the body of a mail or notice template is structured-blocks, JSON text, and that an author places a token in content or in an email (term-content-token, EML-012, NTF-1570, CTK-005, CTK-015). It states no schema for the blocks and no syntax for a token reference, so crates/kernel/src/templates.rs checks that a body is JSON text and that a token expression parses, and cannot check that a template names only tokens that exist (define-mail-template error: A token in the template is undefined), that saving content naming an undefined token is refused (CTK-005), or that a token does not refer to itself through other tokens (CTK-003). Decide the block schema and the token reference (for example a text block node of the kind token with a name) in a decision, state it as types, then add the checks to templates::problems and refuse a bundle at install.
tasks.title: State the block schema of a template and the syntax that places a token in one

acceptance_criteria: node C:/dev/exegra/cli/exegra.js validate of the stacked specification has errors 0 and warnings 0, and apply-change has no uncovered branch

a schema that holds a template, a token, a product record, a ledger declaration and a setting keeps all of them through define-object, define-field and every other arm of apply-change (an example for each)
tasks.description: w3bundle (ops C:/dev/audit-wave/ops/w3bundle.ops.json) replaces the body and the examples of the function apply-change with the body of the base specification plus (1) , mail-templates: schema.mail-templates, notice-templates: schema.notice-templates, tokens: schema.tokens, products: schema.products inserted before the closing brace of every tenant-schema literal (also in schema-with-team and schema-with-invitation) and (2) a final arm _ => try call apply-meta-change(schema, change). w3ledger and w3set replace the same body with arms of their own (declare-ledger-unit, define-setting and the others) and add members to tenant-schema (ledger, settings, capabilities) that every literal must carry on. The three replacements cannot be merged by the coordinator as lists. Merge them: take the base body, insert the members of all three slices in each tenant-schema literal, put the arms of w3ledger and w3set before the final _ arm, and keep the examples of all three. Then run the differential test of crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs.
tasks.title: Reconcile apply-change after the three slices that add schema-change variants

acceptance_criteria: generated_differential.rs no longer lists difference 11 and compares reads of note_by_slug (an index plan) between the hand kernel and kernel_read
spec functions for plan_query and scan_warnings exist with examples covering every plan shape and every scan reason, and Exegra validate reports errors 0, warnings 0
the generated read-needs returns Need::IndexPage for a planned query, equal to strata_kernel::read_needs on the differential corpus
tasks.description: WG-5104 added index plans of named queries in crates/kernel/src/query_plan.rs (plan_query, named_needs, read_named, scan_warnings) and hooked them into crates/kernel/src/read.rs (read, read_needs) and crates/kernel/src/transition.rs (change_schema evidence). The spec functions kernel-read / named-read, read-needs and change-schema in specifications/spec.jsonc still scan every filtered query, refuse an at cursor (query-page-errors) and write no query-plan warning, so crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs carries known difference 11 with guards assert_not_planned and assert_no_scan_warning. Mirror the planner, the index-page candidate walk (bound 1600, cursor rules of KRN-2521/KRN-2522) and the warnings as new spec functions with examples, wire them into the shared bodies, and filter and order on the redacted record (KRN-2522).
tasks.title: Mirror named query index plans into the spec functions and remove differential difference 11

acceptance_criteria: a test with a read policy that follows a reference into a type of 100,000 records shows a named query read loading at most a constant number of records of the referenced type, for the memory store and SQLite
query and load_covering never insert Need::AllOf for a missing single record, and the number of load rounds of such a read is bounded by a constant independent of the page size
tasks.description: crates/storage-api/src/lib.rs query (and crates/storage-api/src/covering.rs load_covering, which mirrors it for views) turn an InsufficientState naming Need::Record into Need::AllOf of that object type, so that a read policy or query filter that follows a reference (Expr::Through) costs one round. Over a large referenced type that loads the whole type for every read, which defeats the bounded loads of WG-5104 (index plans) and KRN-1286 windows. Ask instead for the records the examined rows refer to, e.g. by having the kernel name every missing record of the rows it examined at once (a Need for a set of ids) or by collecting the references of the loaded candidates before evaluation.
tasks.title: Stop query and view loads widening a missing record to its whole object type

acceptance_criteria: a query author == param ordered by a time field descending over 100,000 records loads a bounded number of records per page, with the same rows as a scan, for the memory store and SQLite
the schema change that defines such a query lists no query-plan scan warning for it
tasks.description: WG-5104 index plans (crates/kernel/src/query_plan.rs plan_query) serve an equality or range on the field a query orders by, or an equality ordered by record id. A query such as posts by this author newest first (author == param ordered by published_at or created_at descending) stays a scan, refused above 10,000 records, and the schema change warns of it. Serving it needs a composite key (field value, order value, id) in crates/storage-sqlite/src/index_page.rs and record_index or a new table, a need variant carrying both, and the system attributes $created_at/$updated_at in the index. Decide the storage cost and which pairs are indexed (declared per query at definition time, or every pair of a declared index).
tasks.title: Serve an equality on one field ordered by another from an index

acceptance_criteria: specc generates a conformance test per shipped contract that has a bffRoute, and the gate fails when a shipped contract with a route has none
Each generated test runs against the real BFF, backend and SQLite store, not a mock
For each contract the suite asserts the auth refusals its contract declares, and reply and error shapes against the declared types

acceptance_criteria: A route serving receive-delivery-report accepts a report signed by the configured provider and calls crates/backend/src/dispatch/reports.rs::apply; a test in crates/backend/tests/dispatch.rs shows a forged signature refused as unauthenticated and a report older than five minutes refused as stale-report

specifications/spec.jsonc states the provider's report format and signature scheme in a decision, and receive-delivery-report has deployment shipped
tasks.description: The mail dispatcher (crates/backend/src/dispatch) applies a delivery report through crates/backend/src/dispatch/reports.rs::apply: the five-minute window, the mapping by provider reference '<tenant>:<message id>' (the X-Strata-Message header the dispatcher sets), unmatched references, seven-day dedupe by event id, bounce and complaint suppression. The specification states no format and no signature scheme of the provider's reports (D-523 names Amazon SES; EML-019, EML-1567), so the contract receive-delivery-report (CT-157) is not served: no route reads and verifies a provider report. tasks.title: Mail: delivery report adapter for the configured provider (receive-delivery-report)

acceptance_criteria: Listing the mail log with a filter reads only matching rows through an index, shown by a conformance case in crates/storage-api/src/conformance.rs, and the allowance counter is incremented atomically: a test runs two increments concurrently and reads 2
rec-mail-message, rec-mail-suppression and rec-mail-quota in specifications/spec.jsonc have realisation shipped and the gate's table check passes
tasks.description: crates/backend/src/dispatch/store.rs keeps the mail log, suppressions, allowance counters, categories, seen reports and the breaker as kinds of the store's small-document table (Store::doc_put). Limits: list-mail-messages and count-mail-messages read the whole log (doc_list) and filter in memory; the complaint breaker scans the log once a minute; an allowance counter is read and written back, so two worker passes of one tenant at once can each count a message the other does not see (overshoot by at most the concurrent passes of one tenant); retention runs from the worker at most once an hour per tenant. Add tenant tables (messages indexed by created time, state, category, template, reference and send; suppressions by address hash and category; allowance counters with an atomic increment) to the Store trait (crates/storage-api/src/lib.rs, memory.rs) and crates/storage-sqlite/src/lib.rs with a tenant migration step and conformance cases, and mark rec-mail-message, rec-mail-suppression and rec-mail-quota shipped.
tasks.title: Mail: move the dispatcher's storage from documents to tables with indexes and atomic counters

acceptance_criteria: A bundle that declares a category installs it and the dispatcher reads its purpose from the tenant schema; a test in crates/kernel/tests/object_meta.rs refuses the reserved names and a 51st category
crates/backend/src/dispatch/store.rs no longer holds the kind mail-category and define-message-category answers the schema version

acceptance_criteria: send-message with channel inbox or both creates the inbox notice in the same transaction, and a test shows it listed by list-inbox

acceptance_criteria: A test shows a tenant crossing the 0.1 percent complaint warning receives the notice mail.sending-warning once, and crossing 0.5 percent the notice mail.sending-held

The erasure receipt names the mail log among what was erased

acceptance_criteria: crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/refused has a fixture whose template body is not a list of template-block, one whose link has a javascript: target and one that places a token the product does not define, and specc refuses each with a layer rule that names the template and the place in the body

tasks.title: specc and Exegra refuse a product template whose body is not blocks of the template schema

acceptance_criteria: a test stores a copy of a view with a setting argument for two persons with person-level overrides and the two copies are never shared, and a change of the tenant override gives the copy a new key

list-webhook-deliveries pages without reading every delivery of the tenant (a store query with a limit and a cursor), shown by a test with more entries than one page

acceptance_criteria: A webhook endpoint secret sealed for tenant A cannot be opened with tenant B's key or associated data, shown by a test in crates/backend/tests/outbound.rs

acceptance_criteria: At least 7 class A, 3 class B and 2 class C cases in C:\dev\strata, each with its expected verdict and reason recorded before its first run

Every surprise found is filed as its own Workgraph task with the case that reproduces it

tasks.description:
Repository: strata (C:\dev\strata). Lives in Strata because the cases are about Strata's platform and run against its real specification (specifications/spec.jsonc) as it changes.

A directory of change sets (e.g. specifications/calibration/<case>/ops.json + case.jsonc), each written with its expected outcome BEFORE it is run, and a runner script that runs every case through `exegra admit` (WG-5264) and reports surprises.

Classes:
A. Must be rejected, each aimed at one check, naming the expected reason: a contract reading tenant data without tenant scope; a calls edge closing a dependency cycle through the kernel (needs WG-5263 recursive relations: the first real-world case for them); a state-machine change removing a guard so a model-checked invariant breaks (claim turns violated with a counterexample trace); a product entity claiming platform powers; deleting a type contracts still use; a retention period shorter than a dependent copy's; removing the only evidence of a requirement in a started milestone.
B. Must be admitted, substantial and legitimate, to catch false alarms: a whole new Fieldnotes feature (e.g. scheduled publishing: events, behavior, contract, screen, claims and a scenario); splitting a component in two and moving its contracts; moving a contract from hand-written to generated with the fields that needs.
C. Known blind spots, expected to pass and documented as such: prose contradicting a claim; a claim whose statement and formal check disagree.

Every mismatch between expected and actual verdict is either a verifier bug or a missing rule, and is filed as its own task.
tasks.title: Strata: verifier calibration corpus — substantial spec changes with expected verdicts, run through exegra admit

tasks.description: Strata's generated rule lookup (spec function rule-lookup, used by authorize-needing, redact, named-read and workflow-step since WG-5096) is keyed by reference field, because Exegra's eval lookup (src/core/language-eval.js, WG-4968) has two outcomes only: a field the lookup does not hold is an evaluation error, and a target the field holds no entry for is null. The kernel's Lookup (crates/kernel/src/rules.rs Lookup::record) refuses per record: following a target the snapshot does not cover is an error, following a covered target that does not exist is null. So rule-lookup leaves a field out when the snapshot does not cover its target in both the stored record and the candidate, and a transition rule that follows the covered one of two different targets of one field fails to evaluate where the kernel follows it. This is difference 16 of crates/kernel/tests/generated_differential.rs, guarded by compare_attributed refusing a corpus update that changes a reference. Exegra needs a way for a lookup to say that one target of a field it holds is not covered (for example a reserved entry, or a third map of uncovered targets), evaluated as an error by eval and generated the same way by specc's language bridge (crates/spec-compiler/src/language.rs eval_fn).
tasks.title: Exegra: a lookup of eval that can mark one target of a field as not covered

tasks.description:
Two linked problems with the cloud profile (D-24/D-25):
1. Database-per-tenant on RDS: point-in-time recovery is per instance, not per database, so "point-in-time copies of each tenant database" (backup-archive) needs either an instance per tenant or a custom per-tenant backup pipeline. Thousands of databases per cluster also cost connection pools per database, per-database vacuum and catalogue overhead, and fan-out migrations.
2. D-25 crypto-shredding: destroying a tenant's wrapped data key makes unreadable only data Strata encrypted itself. RDS snapshots, S3 and EBS encrypt with per-instance/per-bucket KMS keys, so a deleted tenant's rows stay readable in managed snapshots until their retention ends.
Decide together: placement tiers (shared database with tenant scoping for small tenants vs dedicated database for large/regulated), the backup mechanism per tier, and what erasure promises each tier can actually keep.
tasks.title: Strata decision: tenant placement tiers, backup and erasure model on managed PostgreSQL

tasks.description:
Umbrella. A tenant's entities depend on each other across authors and products (A <- B <- C, diamonds, cycles). Today the kernel refuses dangling references (schema.rs) and int-2900 protects product-owned entities, but nothing classifies a change by its effect on dependents, adapts them, or lets them stay on an old version. Design (shared by every task of this programme).
1. Dependency graph: every entity (object type, field, query, policy, view, workflow, trigger, automation, screen, form, event kind) lists what it depends on at field level, computed by specc and the kernel, never declared by hand. Products declare product dependencies with a version range (closes S-27, WG-5321).
2. Change algebra: every schema change is classified by its effect on dependents, computed not declared. compatible (add field, widen type, add enum value): every valid dependent stays valid and evaluates the same. adaptable (rename, move field, total split): dependents are rewritten mechanically with identical results. breaking (remove, narrow, retarget a reference, single to list): dependents cannot be fixed automatically; expand/contract applies.
3. Structural versions: an entity's version moves only on a breaking change; dependents pin the versions they were validated against.
4. Projections: a breaking change across an ownership boundary does not break the dependent; it reads through a projection (lens) of the pinned version until migrated or a deprecation window closes (generalises mig-562). An open client running definition v is a dependent pinned to v (live-client-control, WG-5292).
5. Concurrency: changes with disjoint footprints commute; overlapping ones are serialised by the revision guard and the later one's impact is recomputed (rebase).
Lean theorems: (1) closure: accepted changes leave no dangling reference and acyclic definition dependencies; (2) locality: entities outside impact(change) evaluate identically; (3) compatibility; (4) rewrite correctness; (5) lens laws, reversible changes have a left inverse; (6) commutation of disjoint footprints; (7) composition of rewrites; (8) dependency-ordered install and removal; (9) counterexample: a breaking change misclassified as compatible breaks a dependent. General theorems over an abstract model; per-change checks by a verified checker, not kernel decide over data; Lean/Rust correspondence on generated histories.

tasks.description:
Test the live tenant UI update path (a schema notice makes the client re-read the manifest, keep unchanged parts, fetch changed ones and redraw) under hard conditions:
- intertwined features, shared state across users and tabs, and many entity schemas changing at once;
- dependent entities (references read through), out-of-order delivery, disconnects, removals and reinstalls.

Two layers:
- (A) A deterministic simulator in web/test. N tabs run the real kernel (update.js is pure: state and msg in, state and effects out). A fake gateway serves real manifests and parts generated by the substrate from a versioned product family, plus a scheduler that controls delivery order. Invariants are checked after every step, with seeded random interleavings.
- (B) Playwright scenarios against the real dev stack, with several browser contexts for different users.

Invariants:
- I1: a drawn tenant screen's part is listed in the newest manifest the tab accepted.
- I2: a tab's accepted schema_version never decreases.
- I3: after quiescence, every connected tab holds the server's manifest hash.
- I4: no draft value is lost unless its field was removed, and then the loss is shown.
- I5: every submitted operation shows exactly one outcome.
- I6: part fetches per tab per upgrade are at most the changed parts it needs.
- I7: no exception and no effect loop (a bounded number of effects per message).

Scenarios that fail today are recorded as todo with the reason, and feed WG-5332 (managed live reload). Live run on 2026-11-21: a title-only upgrade redrew two tabs without a reload.
