tasks.description:
web/test/support/hot-reload-sim.js:
- Tabs hold the client state from initialState() and step it with update(state, msg) from web/src/kernel/update.js.
- The effects each step returns are routed to a fake gateway. HTTP requests go to /api/ui, /api/ui/parts/:hash, the view models and the operations; socket messages go to welcome, event, resync and the notices.
- The gateway holds the server's state: the installed version's manifest and parts, loaded from web/test/fixtures/hot-reload or given inline, plus records per object, with operations that create and update records and emit notices.
- A scheduler queues every in-flight response and notice per tab. A scenario can deliver them in a chosen order, drop or delay them, disconnect and reconnect a tab, or deliver them all (quiesce).
- Every step calls view() and checks invariants I1-I7 (WG-5344), recording which one fails with the tab, step and message.
- Every tab's drawn page can be read as text, for assertions.

Study web/test/tenant-ui.test.js and web/test/client.test.js for how messages and effects look.

tasks.description:
Each scenario is a test in web/test/hot-reload.test.js named after it. Every step checks I1-I7, and a scenario the client cannot meet today is test.todo naming its gap.

- S1: a title-only upgrade with 2 tabs on the screen. Only the screen part is fetched again; the errors part is not.
- S2: added field. A draft in the open form is kept, and the new field and column appear.
- S3: rename title to subject while tab A holds a draft in title. The draft carries over to subject, and old records show under subject.
- S4: the screen a tab is on is removed. The tab says so, with no error loop and no fetch storm.
- S5: route moved. A tab on the old route follows to the new one, keeping its parameters.
- S6: v2 and v3 back to back, with v2's notice delivered after v3's manifest. The tab ends on v3 and never draws v2 afterwards.
- S7: a part answers 404 because a later upgrade replaced it. The client reads the manifest again and converges.
- S8: socket dropped mid-upgrade, then reconnected with resync. The client converges, and with no change it fetches nothing.
- S9: multi-entity upgrade (v6). A tab on screen X fetches only X's part and errors; navigating to Y then fetches Y's new part.
- S10: dependent chain. The board shows customer.name through the reference; renaming it to display_name keeps the values in the open tab, with no blank column.
- S11: two users. A's operation is in flight when the notice arrives. One outcome is shown, the record appears in B's tab, and nothing is submitted twice.
- S12: a required input is added while a draft is open. Submitting the old draft is refused, worded by the tenant and mapped to the new field.
- S13: an error message is reworded while it is displayed. The text updates.
- S14: live binding kinds changed. The new kind refreshes the screen; the old one no longer does.
- S15: auth tightened to a role. A member's tab shows the refusal state; an editor's tab is unaffected.
- S16: remove and reinstall with the same element ids and different content (ABA). No cached old part is drawn.
- S17: two products, one upgraded. Tabs on the other product fetch no parts and redraw nothing.
- S18: two owners upgrade concurrently. One is refused, and the tabs converge on the accepted one.
- S19: 20 tabs on mixed screens and one upgrade. Part fetches equal the changed parts each tab needs.
- S20: a background tab misses 3 upgrades. On resume it goes straight to the latest, never drawing the ones in between.
- S21: a record created under v1 without the field added in v2. The tab draws it with the default or blank.
- S22: a workflow state added while a record's transition buttons are shown. The buttons update.
- S23: rollback (v3, then v2 re-applied). Tabs converge, and drafts in fields both versions have are kept.
- S24: breaking change (retype) with a pinned client. The client keeps its definition and reads through the projection until reload. This is expected to be a gap, owned by WG-5327/5332.

After the spec-only cut, 149 tests fail on integration 792ae6b, plus a stack overflow in a generated model-core example. The full log is var/failures.log in the stack/fix worktree.

Root causes and their fix groups:
- (A) The BFF and the backend parse a request body before their origin, CSRF and session checks, and refuse a body that is not JSON with a plain-text axum rejection: 120 conformance tests, edge, and hosts_invite x2.
- (B) Tests use hyphenated workflow and role ids that the spec's pattern ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$ refuses (hub, audit_log). The spec is right, since no tenant uses hyphens.
- (C) Test fixtures predate D-6584, retention for personal fields (files x7).
- (D) Product and automation authoring: a trigger naming a ledger unit its own bundle declares is refused; automation keys use undeclared parameters (outbound x2, product_bundle tiers and badge, badge_milestones worker); the products owned-list expectation is stale.
- (E) The dispatch mail template fixture uses an old block shape.
- (F) Purity: OnceLock in kernel ledger_policy.rs and substrate subscribe.rs, and the kernel's allowed dependency list lacks model-core (its generated types).
- (G) The hand-written kernel and the spec function disagree on needs for change_schema (Ledger(Limits)).
- (H) Single kernel and client bugs: erasure is not idempotent, a trigger condition does not ask for the record it lacks, the subject export refusal code is wrong, JS checked arithmetic, and the model-core schema_limit_problems_example_2 stack overflow.
- (I) Stale expectations: the deploy golden after the compose job-count change, the SQLite control migration count, and PostgreSQL tests that panic without STRATA_PG_URL instead of being opt-in.

Requirements exist for: routing by tenant to cell; backend chosen per cell by configuration; tenant move accepted only on matching canonical state hash; backend-specific features not used above the storage port; noisy-neighbour limits per tenant and per cell; per-tenant point-in-time restore on SQLite cells
Backup, point-in-time restore and erasure requirements are stated per backend, and the erasure wording no longer depends on destroying a key that RDS managed backups do not use
ten-014 and every other requirement the decision invalidates are updated in the same change and listed in the commit message

tasks.description:
Specification change only (specifications/spec.jsonc), no code. Decided with the owner 2026-11-21.

Target: each tenant's data is a SQLite file (the existing tenant-file layout), on EC2 with EBS volumes, grouped into cells (a process or host serving a subset of tenants). Litestream streams each tenant file to S3 for point-in-time restore of that one tenant and AZ loss; instance loss reattaches the EBS volume. Not EFS, not Lambda, not ephemeral Fargate storage. Noisy-neighbour isolation: per-tenant quotas in the application for everyone, CPU/memory/IO limits per cell process, gp3 provisioned IOPS per volume, and a dedicated cell for tenants that need a guarantee.

Port: the storage backend is chosen per cell by configuration (sqlite files, or a PostgreSQL connection such as RDS). Three things become explicit boundaries: (1) the control directory (tenant directory, session directory, job wake index, platform settings) is split from the tenant Store and is shared across cells on RDS PostgreSQL or DynamoDB; (2) the gateway routes every request by tenant -> cell, in both backends; (3) a tenant move between cells or backends exports the tenant state, imports it, and is accepted only when the canonical state hashes match. Backup, point-in-time restore and erasure promises are stated per backend and reported through Capabilities, because they differ (per-tenant keys on S3 backups for SQLite cells; instance-level snapshots and PITR on RDS). Nothing above storage-api depends on a backend feature.

Replaces the database-per-tenant-on-PostgreSQL wording (tenant-database, postgres-adapter, ten-014 and the backup/erasure requirements). Answers WG-5286.
tasks.title: Strata spec: SQLite-per-tenant cells on AWS as the storage target, with a backend port so RDS PostgreSQL is a per-cell configuration

tasks.description:
Found fixing the badge-milestones product (WG-5358). In the tenant rule language, eq, ne and the ordering comparisons propagate null, so `x != null` and `x == null` are null for every x. Under kleene and/or, a condition built on them can never be true.

The badge product's trigger used `param.owner != null and ...` and never fired, silently. The language has is_null for this. Per the standing rule (findings become refusals, WG-4948), specc's layer checks and Exegra's expression checks should refuse a comparison whose operand is the null literal, with a message naming is_null.

tasks.description:
Item 1 of docs/working-set.md (strata integration). Crates: crates/storage-api (Store trait, Commit, Receipt, StoreError::Conflict, MemoryStore, execute_guarded, conformance suite), crates/storage-sqlite, crates/storage-postgres, crates/backend callers of commit.

- Generation { nonce: u128, counter: u64 } in a row of its own per tenant (not the tenant row with schema/member JSON); generation(tenant) -> StoreResult<Option<Generation>> reads only that row.
- load_at / load_complete_at return Loaded { state, generation }, the generation read in the same read transaction as the rows; load / load_complete are defined from them. The kernel State type is not changed.
- The counter is raised by every write transaction that changes what load or load_complete returns for the tenant, and by nothing else. Key documents and the hot-set manifest raise nothing.
- The nonce is drawn only at create, restore_snapshot, import and lease acquisition (a store method WS13/WG-5401 calls), never on handle open. A NonceSource is injected at store construction: random in deployment, seeded in tests and the simulator (D19).
- Commit.expected_generation: Option<Generation>, compared in the same write transaction as the base revision; None accepted only with base_revision: None. execute_guarded sets it to the generation of the attempt's first load and restarts the attempt if a later load in the attempt returns another.
- Receipt.generation, including for a tenant-creating commit (the new tenant's first generation, counter 1). StoreError::Conflict carries the generation found.
- The expected generation (and, under a lease, the fence token) on every other counter-raising method. Fence-token column and comparison, unused until WG-5401.
- The generation is kept out of delta_hash, events_hash, JournalEntry and the idempotency request hash.
- No working set yet.

PostgreSQL run: STRATA_PG_URL=postgres://... cargo test -p strata-storage-postgres --test storage_postgres_slow -- --ignored (existing setup in crates/storage-postgres/tests/postgres.rs; role allowed to create databases). Memory and SQLite runs are in the normal suite.

acceptance_criteria: docs/frontend.md states the current frontend with file references, the options weighed for each primitive (Service Worker and Cache API, IndexedDB, workers including SharedWorker versus leader election, Web Components and form-associated elements, Shadow versus light DOM), and one recommended design

The offline design specifies the write queue, idempotency keys, how queued writes are submitted against the server's guarded commits, what happens on conflict (each conflict class and what the person sees), queue durability across reloads and crashes, multi-tab ownership of the queue, and what may not be done offline

The privacy design specifies encryption at rest, key lifetime, sign-out and session-expiry erasure, per-principal partitioning on shared devices, behaviour when permissions change or a data subject is erased while a copy is offline, and storage eviction (Safari's 7-day rule, quota)
A frontend part of the specification is added under specifications/ with requirements that each name the check that holds them, and the spec gate and specc lint pass

lean/Strata/Client*.lean (or a Client/ directory) builds with lake build, no sorry/admit/new axioms, and proves at least: the client cache never serves an entry staler than its last known generation and a read after a confirmed commit returns it; one principal's cached data is never served to another; after sign-out no cached plaintext is readable; a queued offline write is applied at most once and either commits against the generation it was decided on or is reported as a conflict
The kernel runs the specification's uiScenarios headlessly in Node in the plan, with the test approach stated
Follow-up implementation tasks are listed by dependency with testable acceptance criteria, and no time estimates
An adversarial review round finds no confirmed finding that blocks the first implementation item
tasks.description: Owner request 2026-11-21. Design the Strata frontend to use the browser's own primitives with no third-party runtime libraries (vanilla JS; Vite stays as the build tool; dev-only tools such as Playwright, axe and tsc stay). Build on what exists: the pure kernel in a dedicated Web Worker (web/src/kernel, update/view, effects), generated platform screens, hash-addressed tenant UI parts (D-8250). The client cache mirrors the backend working set (docs/working-set.md): stamped entries, coherence with the server's tenant generation. Storage layering: Service Worker + Cache API for content-addressed assets, IndexedDB for stamped records and view results, worker memory for the hot set. Multi-tab: one leader owns the socket and cache (BroadcastChannel, Web Locks). Web Components (form-associated custom elements) as renderers only. Offline is in scope as a full design: reads from cache and writes queued while offline and reconciled on reconnect against guarded commits (expected generation, idempotency keys), with conflict handling. Privacy at rest: encrypted IndexedDB under a non-extractable WebCrypto session key, sign-out crypto-erases, per-principal partitioning, permission changes invalidate, erasure (D-350) behaviour for offline copies. Correctness never depends on the cache. The kernel stays pure and runs the uiScenarios headlessly in Node. Zero runtime dependencies: replace uqr and self-host fonts.
tasks.title: Strata frontend: deep design and spec for a vanilla browser client (worker kernel, Cache API, IndexedDB, Web Components, offline writes), with Lean proofs and adversarial review

tasks.description:
Consolidated on 2026-11-22 from 20 tasks (the replaced tasks are linked as duplicates and keep their history). Each section below is one part of this work.

## Exegra checks: retry-event attempt cap and parse-refusal cases of the shared language table

Two small Exegra validation gaps: a retry-event with attempts at or above the runtime cap on an implementation-level machine is not refused (WG-5126; the singleton-key half is done at exegra src/core/readiness-machines.js:322), and kernel-cases.json has no parse section, so the Rust, JavaScript and Exegra parsers are not held to the same refusals and texts, notably the number literal beyond 2^53-1 (WG-5144).

Replaces: WG-5126, WG-5144.

## Exegra and specc refusal rules found by audits

Each audit finding becomes a mechanical refusal with a negative fixture. Exegra: refuse a contract delivering a subject's personal data without a step-up (WG-5206); refuse a mail send contract without idempotency key, category input and header-break refusal (WG-5222); refuse a stored copy of tenant records with no sealed-or-expiry erasure point (WG-5250); accept the product section eventKinds (event-kind-decl) with rule layer.event-kind-invalid (WG-5270); accept object-valued vocabulary properties and check conformanceExample against the contract's inputs (WG-5260). specc and Exegra: refuse a product template whose body is not blocks of the template schema (WG-5234).

Replaces: WG-5206, WG-5222, WG-5250, WG-5270, WG-5260, WG-5234.

## Exegra and specc checker gaps: new refusals and Strata-side parity tests

Checker work in Exegra and specc surfaced while building Strata: (WG-5363) refuse a comparison with the null literal in a rule expression, it never holds; (WG-5366) refuse a contract whose auth has csrf or origin but declares no forbidden error; (WG-5120) product-expression checker lacks the rule language's checked arithmetic and time operators; (WG-4883) retention that keeps for a duration after an event, not from creation; (WG-4955) route.ambiguous, the {expr, simulate} timer check, two stale docs; (WG-5350) layered refusal parity for all 41 refused product fixtures in Exegra's own tests; (WG-5041) browser app reloads product files and CI can register the Strata project; (WG-5037) two Exegra tests assert the live Strata spec has no readiness diagnostics (it reports 48 function-branch gaps, to be re-measured after WG-5379 retires the transcribed functions). Each refusal gets a negative fixture.

Replaces: WG-4883, WG-4955, WG-5037, WG-5041, WG-5120, WG-5350, WG-5363, WG-5366.

## Verifier quality programme: calibration corpus, mutation scoring, grounded Harbourline fold

Measure how well exegra admit judges Strata changes. WG-5265: a directory of change sets with expected verdicts (specifications/calibration does not exist yet) run through admit. WG-5266: random breakages of the specification and the fraction admit rejects. WG-5279: redo the Harbourline fold for the fold-only requirements on a throwaway branch under strengthened admit.

Replaces: WG-5265, WG-5266, WG-5279.

## Exegra: accept product.version and product.platform in the product header

specc layers.rs (crates/spec-compiler/src/layers.rs check_header, WG-5080) now accepts the header keys version and platform and validates them: version is three whole numbers joined by dots (is_version); platform is an object with min (a platform release: one to three whole numbers, optionally a hyphen and a label) and optionally below (a release later than min, numbers compared without trailing zeros), no other key; a malformed one is layer.header-invalid, the messages are in platform_problems. Exegra layers.js (C:/dev/exegra/src/core/layers.js) refuses any header key but id, name, description and imports. It must take version and platform with the same validation and the same rule code, and its fixtures (tests/fixtures/layers/refused of Exegra) need a negative one each: a version 1.0, a platform with no min, and a platform whose below is not later than min. The specc fixtures are crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/refused/header-version-invalid.jsonc and header-platform-invalid.jsonc, and the fixtures badge-milestones.jsonc and promotions.jsonc now carry version and platform in their headers, so Exegra refuses them until it takes the keys.

Replaces: WG-5174.

tasks.description:
Consolidated on 2026-11-22 from 8 tasks (the replaced tasks are linked as duplicates and keep their history). Each section below is one part of this work.

## Rule language reads (balance, in_segment, setting) and the promotions fixture that needs them

The tenant rule language has no reads of the ledger balance, segment membership or settings (D-6543), so crates/spec-compiler/tests/fixtures/products/promotions.jsonc leaves out segment eligibility, the per-person limit and per-promotion stock. Land the three reads in order: Exegra catalogue and evaluator (WG-5268), specc, kernel (WG-5269), then restore the fixture. Overlaps WG-5268 and WG-5269 in another chunk; the coordinator may fold this group into WG-5269.

Replaces: WG-5088, WG-5062.

## Rule language reads: balance, in_segment and setting

D-6543 to D-6545 add balance(unit, scope), in_segment(name) and setting(name) to the tenant rule language. Exegra has none of the primitives (checked at C:/dev/exegra: no ledger-balance, segment-member or setting-value in src/core/language.js) (WG-5268); then Strata needs spec expr variants, specc primitives and emission, the kernel Expr and Need (rule_reads.rs says in_segment is not there) and product-file parsing (WG-5269). The kernel type round-trip test crates/spec-compiler/tests/kernel_types.rs must then build ArgSource::Setting and decode template blocks (WG-5236). Order: Exegra first, then specc, kernel, spec entries.

Replaces: WG-5268, WG-5269, WG-5236.

## Ledger: reader-visible balance and expiry chain restart

read_balance answers only when the policies permit the whole account without reading entry fields (D-7880); CT-288 asks for the sum of the entries the reader may read, which needs the entries loaded and a rule for ranking accounts by a derived balance within the scan bound (WG-5254). If a ledger expiry job fails for good or the chain is cancelled by hand, nothing restarts it: the route expire and declare-unit of a unit that already has an expiry should create the job when none is waiting (WG-5256; ledger.rs ledger-expiry:start).

Replaces: WG-5254, WG-5256.

## Settings: float and declared types, and views, dispatcher and live pages that depend on a setting

The kernel value algebra (Value) has no float and the kernel holds no registry of declared types, so crates/kernel/src/settings.rs accepts the setting types bool, i64, string and timestamp only and refuses f64 and the id of a declared id, scalar or enum type (D-5046, SET-001). Also not built: the view argument that takes its value from a setting (arg-source setting, SET-1540), the copy key and audience class that depend on the setting revisions (SET-050, SET-052, SET-053), the mail dispatcher and notification service call of resolve-setting-for (SET-1541), and the refresh of open pages (SET-041; crates/substrate/src/subscribe.rs delivers Notice::Setting but no page reads it).

Replaces: WG-5142.

tasks.description:
Consolidated on 2026-11-22 from 14 tasks (the replaced tasks are linked as duplicates and keep their history). Each section below is one part of this work.

## Notification service: subscriptions, platform notices, mail copy, settings and storage

The in-app inbox is built (crates/backend/src/inbox.rs, inbox/digest.rs; digests landed in f8d55a60) but its header still lists what is not built. Remaining: (1) subscribe-notifications (CT-181), rec-subscription and a topic filter on the Inbox socket message (WG-5188). (2) Platform-produced notices for the six platform topics (approval.requested/decided, form.submitted, file.scan-finished, mail.sending-warning, mail.sending-held) with their fixed recipient sets; no platform code calls inbox::deliver (WG-5190); owner notices from the mail breaker and the mail-delivered/bounced/complained/unsubscribed domain events (WG-5219). (3) The mail copy of a notice: inbox::request_mail_copy still answers 'mail delivery not wired'; make it create the mail job and honour the mail-channel preference and mute (WG-5191; the category store is already shared, 60be8615). (4) Ship the settings time-zone, quiet-hours and mute-until (PLATFORM_SETTINGS in crates/kernel/src/settings.rs is empty), a zone database in place of the fixed-offset reader, and release pushes deferred by quiet hours (WG-5192). (5) Inbox storage: index by recipient instead of listing and paging a whole inbox in memory, and commit inbox-notice-read and ev-inbox-item-ended as domain events instead of a log line (WG-5193; end_for_erasure already ends items at an erasure).

Replaces: WG-5188, WG-5190, WG-5191, WG-5192, WG-5193, WG-5219.

## Mail dispatcher: delivery reports, storage, categories, inbox channel and subject erasure

The mail dispatcher (crates/backend/src/dispatch) serves templated sends but: (1) receive-delivery-report (CT-157) is not served: the provider's report format and signature need a decision, then an adapter that parses and verifies a report and calls reports::apply, a route for the mail-provider role, and deployment shipped (WG-5215). (2) Storage is the small-document table: the log is listed whole and filtered in memory, allowance counters are read-modify-write; move to tables with indexes and an atomic counter on the Store trait and both adapters (WG-5216; shares the atomic counter with the quota group). (3) define-message-category keeps categories in dispatcher documents; the contract says tenant metadata versioned with the schema, via schema changes define/remove-message-category, a categories table in TenantSchema and checks in the style of templates::problems (WG-5217). (4) send-message refuses the inbox and both channels and a delivery time, and leasing has no class priority sign-in, transactional, bulk (WG-5218). (5) erase-subject does not know the mail log: remove or anonymise a subject's entries by principal and verified address and name the mail log in the receipt (WG-5220).

Replaces: WG-5215, WG-5216, WG-5217, WG-5218, WG-5220.

## Webhooks: expiry, tenant-keyed secrets, and removal

Outbound and inbound webhook documents (crates/backend/src/outbound) are never expired: delivery log entries should lapse after thirty days and remembered inbound event ids after seven (needs a doc purge or a dedicated table), and list_deliveries pages in memory (WG-5237). Webhook secrets are sealed under the platform factor key, not a key of the tenant as INT-1578 says; either introduce per-tenant data keys or change INT-1578 (WG-5238; owner decision tied to the key work in the erasure group). No contract or route removes a subscription or inbound endpoint although the removal events and erasure points exist (WG-5240).

Replaces: WG-5237, WG-5238, WG-5240.

tasks.description:
Consolidated on 2026-11-22 from 7 tasks (the replaced tasks are linked as duplicates and keep their history). Each section below is one part of this work.

## Files: delivery and acceptance safety (file domain, readable-file check, scanner, renditions)

(1) Uploaded files are served by GET /files/... mounted on every host and resolved from the host; CMS-258 and CMS-259 want a configured file host in the BFF Config, the tenant carried in the signed address and the route mounted only there (WG-5224). (2) The kernel accepts any string in a file field; mutate-record must check each written file value with files::access::may_read and the file state before commit (WG-5229). (3) Only DevScanner exists and delivery reads files up to 100 MiB into memory; add a configured scanner adapter (clamd) and stream bodies (WG-5230). (4) Rendition jobs fail for good because no image library is a dependency; run renditions in a sandboxed process with no secret and no network (WG-5227).

Replaces: WG-5224, WG-5229, WG-5230, WG-5227.

## Files: domain events, tenant limits and the erasure receipt

The events file-scanned and rendition-ready exist only as telemetry lines (crates/model/records/src/telemetry.rs says the EventBody variants are 'to be added'); commit them as kernel events from the scan and rendition jobs so a trigger can wait (WG-5223). files::tenant_limits ignores its arguments and returns platform limits (files/mod.rs:235); wire it to stored tenant-settings.files (WG-5225). erase_subject binds the removed files to _files (erasure.rs:330); put their ids in Receipt.reached and drop the not_reached line (WG-5228).

tasks.description:
Consolidated on 2026-11-22 from 14 tasks (the replaced tasks are linked as duplicates and keep their history). Each section below is one part of this work.

## Privacy: restriction of processing, legal hold, retention default and subject export

Restriction (PRV-352) is enforced in views, search, retention, receipt and export but nowhere else (grep restrict in crates/backend/src): automations still start for a restricted person's records (worker/steps.rs start_run; needs an automation-exception-reason value) (WG-5200); segments still evaluate and enter a restricted person and the erased set cannot carry a lifted restriction (WG-5201); aggregates, named queries and mail to addresses in personal fields ignore restriction (WG-5202). Retention sweeps only types with a rule and does not read retention-default-days (PRV-356), and creation or last-change rules page the whole type (WG-5204). Legal hold covers a subject or type, not named records (PRV-355) (WG-5205). Subject export assembles from load_complete (unbounded) and omits federated identities; needs Store::identities_of and owner-keyed reads (WG-5203).

Replaces: WG-5200, WG-5201, WG-5202, WG-5203, WG-5204, WG-5205.

## Erasure, sealing, keys and restore: close the gaps where personal data or destroyed keys survive

(1) The sealed store seals only create-record and update-record fields; operation inputs, invitation addresses, job and run parameters and person-level setting overrides stay plain in the journal (WG-5245). (2) A restore re-applies neither key destructions nor erasure receipts recorded after its point (D-7727, D-6206) (WG-5246). (3) The audit chain head is not anchored outside the tenant database, so removal of the newest lines is undetected; verify-audit-chain itself is now served at POST /internal/audit/verify (crates/backend/src/audit_log.rs), only the anchor remains (WG-5247). (4) export-tenant must carry sealed fields and wrapped keys only (WG-5248). (5) Tenant keys are not re-wrapped when the process key rotates and SEC-251 tenant key rotation is not built (WG-5249). (6) Erasure of an invoker does not remove tenant-operation run rows (tbl-idempotency, principal|op:<operation>; erasure.rs:297 still says 24 hours) (WG-5251). (7) No test shows the real erasure path ending segment memberships with sealed exit events and no re-entry (WG-5233).

Replaces: WG-5245, WG-5246, WG-5247, WG-5248, WG-5249, WG-5251, WG-5233.

## Erasure: delete records whose retention has ended, and resolve subject fields that reference a person record

crates/kernel/src/erasure.rs clears personal fields and never deletes a record, and it cannot match a subject field typed as a reference to the record of a person (it reports it in not-erased). PRV-357 deletes records whose retention has ended with the reach of an erasure; the retention job is not built.

Replaces: WG-5116.

acceptance_criteria: Two backend processes sharing a database cannot together exceed a short-window or long-window limit, shown by a concurrent test

tasks.description:
Consolidated on 2026-11-22 from 23 tasks (the replaced tasks are linked as duplicates and keep their history). Each section below is one part of this work.

## Plan quotas: shared counters, plan data, and every creator of jobs, mail and files counted

crates/backend/src/quota.rs enforces request quotas and keeps plan allowances as code. Remaining: (1) windows of a minute or less are counted per process and longer windows are read, decided and written without a database lock; use one atomic count per quota and scope key in the store and move the sign-in rate onto it (WG-5195). (2) plan_allowance holds the D-508/D-700/SEG-029 numbers as code; make plan allowances data in the specification (plan.allowances, which needs an Exegra metamodel property) and generate the table (WG-5196). (3) Jobs created by the worker for the next step and by segment batches and refreshes bypass JobAdmitter; segment_work.rs keeps a process-wide daily quota table instead of the plan's; jobs past quota should be created due next quota day with a held record (WG-5197, WG-5232). (4) The mail dispatcher never calls quota::mail_admit/mail_sent/mail_used (no caller outside quota.rs) (WG-5198). (5) Requests a second and connections per plan at the gateway, and the BFF aggregate rate (WG-5199). (6) Uploads check only platform, tenant and field caps, not the plan's stored bytes (WG-5231).

Replaces: WG-5195, WG-5196, WG-5197, WG-5198, WG-5199, WG-5232, WG-5231.

## Enterprise-size bounds: state every cap as a plan value, raise the ones that block, enforce the rest

Caps still in code (crates/kernel/src/limits.rs, segments.rs:70-85): 200 object types, 100 fields, 500 policies and queries (S-2, plus a linear policy scan per authorization), MAX_SCAN_RECORDS 10,000 for aggregates and scans (S-5), 100 segments and 25 per type (S-6), 100 triggers in code and a function description only and 32 event kinds (S-7), content caps of 64 KB string, 256 KB record, 200 KB Markdown (S-19), 100 MiB video master (S-20), reference chains of 32 rounds with no stated outcome (S-21), search 1,000 candidates in unstated order (S-22), unbounded export and archive and mismatched batch sizes (S-26), plan quotas that do not bound entities, policies, segments, triggers, roles, teams, users (S-17) and nothing bounding workflows, views, templates, tokens, invitations (S-18), segment restores, predicate changes and time-dependent refreshes beyond the daily job quota (S-15, S-16; seg-1544 versus seg-021, seg-023 not parsing as a count).

Replaces: WG-5296, WG-5299, WG-5300, WG-5301, WG-5309, WG-5310, WG-5311, WG-5312, WG-5313, WG-5314, WG-5315, WG-5316, WG-5320.

## Connection admission and event fan-out capacity

WG-5303: BFF admission is keyed by source address (bff/src/limits.rs:26-27, 32 sockets per source), so one NAT'd enterprise is limited in total; authenticated traffic should be per session or principal. WG-5304: event fan-out costs connections x subscriptions x (teams + policies), visibility recomputed per connection. WG-5305: 2,048 connections per process with a per-process registry (runtime/src/server.rs:240), relay queues bound messages not bytes. Overlaps WG-5199 and WG-5287 (other chunks).

Replaces: WG-5303, WG-5304, WG-5305.

## Web client screens for shipped server features: inbox, file uploader, mail subscription page, webhook pages

The server side exists and the web client has no screen for it. (a) Inbox: routes POST /api/inbox/{list,count,read,remove,preferences,templates} (crates/bff/src/routes.rs INBOX_ROUTES) and the ServerMessage::Inbox socket message are built; web/ has no inbox view, unread badge, filter by state and topic, mark read/unread, remove, or per-category preferences (WG-5185's text said the routes were missing; they now exist). (b) Uploader: /api/files/upload, /uploads/start, chunks, finish and /files/sign exist (crates/bff/src/files.rs); no web module calls them, so a file field cannot be filled (WG-5186 and WG-5226 are the same work). (c) /mail/subscription page for unsubscribe and resubscribe links (POST /api/mail/subscription exists). (d) Pages for webhook endpoints, subscriptions, secret-once display, rotation and the delivery log. Follow the existing pattern: screen and contracts from the spec, generated into web/src/generated, a kernel module under web/src/kernel wired with one hook in update.js, each control labelled and counts announced through the live region.

Replaces: WG-5185, WG-5189, WG-5186, WG-5226, WG-5221, WG-5239.

## Tenant UI and product upgrades: list rows, role-restricted screens, columns, field rename

WG-5342: a list screen draws each row as stacked raw field names and values instead of a titled row; WG-5352: a screen's auth is only none or session (a role is refused as bundle.ui-unsupported, bundle_ui.rs:45), a list screen has no columns, a view cannot include a field read through a reference; WG-5351: plan_upgrade (substrate/src/product.rs) turns a rename into RemoveField plus DefineField, losing data, so a rename should be a first-class change.

## Live client control at enterprise scale: UI definition updates, pinned clients, notices

WG-5332 folds live client control into schema evolution: an open browser running UI definition v is a dependent pinned to v, updated by rewrite (adaptable) or reload/projection (breaking); needs the tenant UI install path (WG-5297, other chunk). WG-5302: every schema or setting notice refreshes every bound screen whole and resync re-reads everything. Consolidated on 2026-11-22 from 7 tasks (the replaced tasks are linked as duplicates and keep their history). Each section below is one part of this work.

## Request edge uses the generated boundary, with the aggregate source quota

The BFF and backend authorize, parse and validate with hand-written code while specc's generated routes, authorizer, contracts and records are linked by no running code (WG-5183, WG-5184: crates/model/records and target-machines hold tens of thousands of unused lines). The conformance suite (WG-5182) already exercises the contracts; this puts the generated layer in the path and removes or justifies what stays unused.

Replaces: WG-5122, WG-5183, WG-5184.

## Generated routes and specification statements that disagree with the backend

WG-4893: generated routes per contract; the error status per kind is now generated (routes.rs:2227 errorKinds map), remaining are per-contract serving instead of per component, the app's error body and auth. WG-5359: D-6523 says an inbound-webhook trigger binds endpoint, event_id and body while CT-172 and backend/outbound/inbound.rs:353 pass webhook_event, webhook_endpoint, webhook_body; pick one and make spec, code and tests agree. WG-5361: send-digest-step says no recipient means everyone holding a notice of the category, D-8200 and digest.rs say every tenant member; pick one.

## Extend the bffRoute vocabulary to methods, wildcard segments and path parameters

The property bffRoute of a contract accepts only GET or POST and a path (crates/spec-compiler/src/web_kernel.rs parse_route), and the web kernel sends the path as written. The BFF mounts ANY /scim/v2/*rest (SCIM: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE), GET and POST /api/identity/*action (clients, keys/rotate, keys/compromise, grants, provisioning/tokens, provisioning/groups), GET /api/lab/runs/:id, GET /federation/saml/metadata/:provider and POST /api/dev/:action. WG-5049..5052 declared what the vocabulary can: provision-user names POST /scim/v2/Users, list-identity-clients GET /api/identity/clients, create-grant, revoke-grant and rotate-client-secret name their identity routes, and read-lab-run, serve-saml-metadata and run-development-action name the router pattern with :id, :provider and :action written literally. The other SCIM verbs and identity actions (keys/rotate, keys/compromise, clients/create, clients/revoke, provisioning/tokens/create, provisioning/tokens/revoke, provisioning/groups, provisioning/groups/set, provisioning/groups/remove) have no contract. Files: crates/spec-compiler/src/web_kernel.rs, scripts/gate-bff-routes.mjs, specifications/spec.jsonc (vocabulary property bffRoute).

Replaces: WG-5072.

tasks.description:
Consolidated on 2026-11-22 from 6 tasks (the replaced tasks are linked as duplicates and keep their history). Each section below is one part of this work.

## Search in views and storage conformance

The publication template still answers /search with the scanning named query search_posts (tenants/_templates/publication.json:184,259) because a view section can only name a named query; add a search section that takes the request's q as its words, use kernel::search::run, and drop search_posts (WG-5207). Store::search_candidates is compared between MemoryStore and SqliteStore only in crates/storage-sqlite/tests/search.rs; the shared storage-api conformance suite has no case (WG-5209).

Replaces: WG-5207, WG-5209.

## Copy store: aggregate and view copies shared, single-flight and keyed by settings

Aggregate copies live in the memory of one process (Copies on App, crates/backend/src/aggregates.rs) and simultaneous first requests each compute the result (CPY-012); copies are not dropped by tag on erasure (CPY-013). No view copy store exists in the backend (no put-copy or get-copy), so strata_kernel::settings::copy_dependencies is unused; when the store exists a view copy whose sections name a setting must carry key_part() of each dependency and must not be shared when shareable() is false (SET-052, SET-053). Build one copy store used by both aggregate and view copies.

Replaces: WG-5194, WG-5235.

## Strata: push query filters down to the store

Named queries currently load every record of their object type (Need::AllOf) and filter in the kernel. Correct but O(records) per read. Gap noted in docs/storage.md under Limits.

Replaces: WG-4813.

## Bound pair pages by a range on the order attribute

crates/kernel/src/query_plan.rs plan_query (WG-5181) serves field == value ordered by another attribute from Need::PairPage, but a query that also bounds the order attribute (promotion == p and redeemed_at > t ordered by redeemed_at) is served by the range plan on redeemed_at (all promotions), and the pair plan, when chosen, walks every record of the value because Need::PairPage carries no bounds on the order value. Add lower/upper bounds on the order key to Need::PairPage (spec type need, crates/storage-sqlite/src/pair_index.rs pair_page, query_plan::pair_page), prefer the bounded pair plan over the range plan when an equality on another field exists, and mirror the variant change in the spec functions covers and need-order.

Replaces: WG-5244.

(WG-5287) per-process state breaks with more than one replica: the quota window is an in-memory Mutex map (crates/backend/src/quota.rs:139), files are in a local directory; move behind shared-store adapters. ## Control plane generated from the spec: tenant directory, provisioning, suspend, export, restore, delete, domain binding

## Field-level read permissions and opaque principal ids

Read authorization is per record, not per field. Author records expose a principal field (for example user:ines, equal to the login name) to anonymous visitors, used by the web to preselect the author. An author can also set another author's record on their own post because policy conditions cannot follow a reference. Fix by field-level read policies in the kernel, or by opaque principal ids.

Replaces: WG-4815, WG-4953.

acceptance_criteria: Every answer to a request (pong or reply) carries the tenant epoch tag and its ordinal, the generation, the erasure epochs of the object types concerned, the floor generation (the greater of the principal's access generation and the tenant's policy generation) current when sent, and the nonce the request carried; a reply also carries the stamp it was read at; view replies are sent Cache-Control: no-store

The tenant epoch ordinal is set at every nonce rotation (restore, re-creation, lease acquisition, import) to max(previous + 1, rotation time in milliseconds) and persisted with the nonce; tests check the new ordinal exceeds every ordinal the tenant's host name has served after each of: a restore from an older snapshot, a control-directory restore, a tenant deleted and re-created on the same host name (Generation::first restarts at 1), and an import into another cell carrying an older ordinal; the rate of rotations under lease failover is measured, since each resets every connected client's cache

Erasure epochs are per object type, derived from a destruction log keyed by object type and sealed field; a key destruction raises, in its transaction, the epoch of every type with a field sealed under the destroyed key, and no other (negative test); no audience class is enumerated

Conformance case for C5: for a view that joins or follows references, destroying a key changes the reply's epoch vector if and only if a sealed field the view opens changes, including fields a Read policy or a derivation reads (relies on depends_on being complete, CPY-004)
A read that opens a sealed field takes the epochs before or atomically with opening: a test destroying a key between the epoch read and the open finds the reply stamped with the old epoch

Exactly these events raise the tenant policy generation, in their transaction: a change of a Read policy, and a change of the definition of a team or role a policy reads; team membership changes, role grants and revocations, restrictions (PRV-352) and permission changes raise only the access generation of the principals concerned (negative test: adding a team member leaves the policy generation unchanged); the purge rate of both is measured

The server pushes a heartbeat frame on each connection every interval; frames carry from, their own stamp, and every key touched in (from, to]; a reconnect with after=seq replays from the generation recorded with that event, or answers resync

A role or membership change notifies every subscriber whose visible set it may alter, including principals other than the subject: when a Read policy depends on who shares a team, adding or removing a member notifies every member of that team whose visible set changes (test: removing B from team T notifies A, whose view of B's records shrinks); a restriction sends a restriction notice

A commit to an object type a view's Read policies follow sends a frame naming the type with no record id, coalesced per connection within a window (at most one such frame per window under load, measured); while a commit is deferred, every frame sent on the connection names the union of what is deferred over its interval or holds its to below the deferred commit (test: commit to a followed type, then a heartbeat sent before the window ends names that type)

A view whose policies read the clock or whose query cannot be resolved is marked volatile by the aggregates/audience classifier less its principal condition; a view that reads neither the clock nor a reference is not volatile (negative test)

Lookup fence: a lookup of an uncommitted idempotency key records a tombstone kept for the key's idempotency retention, scoped to the tenant, principal and contract, and checked in the same store transaction as the commit; a submission of that key held up past the gateway deadline is refused (test with a delayed original after a not-found lookup). Letting the tombstone expire at retention relies on the client never sending a key past its retention, which a client clock set back could break; the client measures retention on the server's clock
Publication evaluates visibility with the schema and members recorded with the event; every out-of-commit write sends resync
docs/protocol.md lists all seven notice kinds, the restriction notice and the stamp fields

acceptance_criteria: Kernel tests written from FE-001, FE-009, FE-002, FE-003, FE-012, FE-015, FE-018 and FE-019's wording pass: current only at the known stamp and within the contact bound; 'checked' (not refetched) at the known stamp past it; older labelled; a reply at the current stamp read back as current; a new erasure epoch for a type deletes that type's view results; a new floor deletes entries read below it; a late put below the floor or of an older epoch is dropped

The floor is the greater of the principal's access generation and the tenant's policy generation: a policy-generation rise purges entries read before it for a principal whose access generation did not change

Tenant epochs: the kernel keeps, with its epoch, the send time of the request whose answer made it switch. It switches on (a) a higher ordinal, or (b) an answer, matched by its echoed nonce, to a request sent after its last switch, carrying a different tag, whatever its ordinal; switching purges every entry and resets known generation, floor and erasure epochs together in one transaction; anything else of another tag (a frame, or an answer to an earlier request, of a lower or equal ordinal) is ignored; no list of left epochs is kept. Tests: the schedule epoch 2, then a late epoch 1 to an earlier request, then epoch 2 ends current in epoch 2; a client at ordinal 5000 reaches a re-created tenant at ordinal 1 through an answer to a later request; two tags at one ordinal (split brain) resolve to the holder that answered the latest request; a re-created tenant's replies at low generations are kept after the reset

Unanswered nonces are garbage-collected: a pending nonce is dropped when its request is answered, abandoned, or older than the contact bound, so the pending set stays bounded (test: a run of unanswered requests leaves at most the requests younger than the contact bound pending); an answer echoing a dropped nonce is not a contact

Carry-forward: a frame from a to b carries forward every entry read in [a, b] whose key it does not name, and drops those read in [a, b] that it names; an entry fetched between two heartbeats is carried by the next one (test on a busy schedule)

A contact is the answer to a request (pong or reply), dated by the request's send time, taken only when the answer echoes the nonce of that request; view reads are issued with cache: 'no-store'; a frame does not refresh the contact; a replayed answer with a stale nonce is not a contact (negative test); a fresh reply under a missing pong does not cause a second request
The leader pings on welcome, and relays contact times to followers as epoch times
A visibility message, and the first message after a gap in timers, re-reads the time and re-evaluates current before the render is posted
After signing in again, nothing from the partition is decrypted or drawn before the first answer's stamp, floor and epoch have been applied
The kernel imports no storage, crypto or network API (source scan test)
New frontend requirements for the kernel declare these web tests as checks and the evidence check passes them

acceptance_criteria: Enrolment issues a device id and a 256-bit device secret; the identity service keeps the share and a hash of the secret, sealed at rest; the browser keeps the device id and secret in the clear in the partitions store (not under a key derived from the share), and after a reload in online-keyed mode it fetches the share with them

POST /api/session/device-key returns the share only to a session of the enrolled principal presenting the right secret; naming the id without it gets nothing (gateway test); request token required; rate limited per session and per device id
After online and offline sign-out, no IndexedDB record of the principal decrypts with any key present, and a session of the same principal elsewhere that knows the device id cannot fetch the share

No WebCrypto call runs inside an IndexedDB transaction; every write is encrypted outside and committed in one short transaction that checks the partition's current key id and, for a write depending on an earlier read, the record's version (compare-and-swap), and is refused and retried otherwise

Rotation in the stated order (new share durable, switch the current key id, re-encrypt each record by compare-and-swap, delete the old share only when the key id is new and no record is under the old key): a crash injected at each step loses no record; a tab holding the old key id that appends after the switch is refused and retries; another tab's rewrite during the pass is not overwritten
A revoked device's records are unreadable after a reload; other devices keep theirs; signing out everywhere revokes all with a confirmation that says unsent work is destroyed

Records persist the stamp they were read at; the additional data binds principal tag, store, key and erasure epoch only, so a heartbeat rewrites nothing on disk (test counting IndexedDB writes over heartbeats)
Every put checks and raises the persisted known stamp and floor of the current tenant epoch, and drops a put of an older epoch, below the floor, or of another tenant epoch
Keeping keys in IndexedDB is off by default and refused unless the realm opts in
A restore of the identity database does not bring back a share or secret deleted after the restore point

tasks.description: Owner decisions 2026-11-22: a neutral base design system with full tenant theming through tokens (Fieldnotes becomes one theme), and tenants can arrange layouts. Motivation: the showcase tenant (WG-5454) rendered as unstructured label/value text because the platform has no component library, no display types and no layout system; the generic interpreter (web/src/kernel/tenant-ui.js) draws views as fields. The platform is meant to be agentic: an agent reads the backend specification and the frontend specification, composes whatever combination of data and screens a tenant asks for, configures it, and the tenant watches it being built live. Wireframing is a first-class concept: an agent first produces a low-fidelity structural wireframe (regions, templates, pattern placeholders bound to data), which renders at once, and refines it to full fidelity. Vanilla JS, Web Components, no third-party runtime libraries, Vite kept; builds on the frontend engine design (docs/frontend.md, WG-5415).

While staging, every other upgrade, removal or draft set touching the product is refused with upgrade.in-progress except the owner abandon (step-up, exempt), which removes everything the stages created, the staging role included, and restores the record at the version installed before the job (test)
An owner may pre-authorise abandon-then-apply for security-tagged upgrades, and a stopped job past its approval period is abandoned automatically, recorded and notified (tests)
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457), "The 200-change cap" (D-DS-16). plan_install splits a product over the cap into <version>-stage.N upgrades, each at most 200 changes and a complete installed version; resumable; the cap and the all-or-none product change unchanged.

acceptance_criteria: tests/corpus/showcase holds no JavaScript, CSS or HTML beyond live.mjs and the agent build script; the four products use only catalogue entries and their own composites

tests/e2e/showcase.spec.js, in the pinned environment, visits every showcase screen as tenant admin, member and anonymous (public screens), in the neutral and fieldnotes themes, light and dark, phone and desk, and compares with owner-accepted baselines
axe at WCAG 2.2 AA reports no violation on any of those pages
No page shows text matching an epoch (\b1\d{12}\b), a principal (\buser:), a JSON object ({") or a record id outside a code display, and no form asks for a record number

A member navigation has no admin entry; a member at /admin gets the same status and text as an unknown address; no byte served to a member names an admin-only element or error message; the moderator message page has the hide action and the member page has none

The agent build script builds the tenant through public routes by writing drafts, a screenshot of the preview after each write showing a valid draft, and publishes by the owner upgrade of an approved revision; the tenant schema version is unchanged before the publish, and members are served nothing new and notified of nothing before it

acceptance_criteria: Every human-readable string prop in the catalogue has the type text (a string or a map of language tags with a default); specc refuses a string prop of another type in a catalogue entry (fixture)
The interpreter picks the request language, then the tenant default language, then default, for every text value (kernel table test)
The root element carries dir and lang from the request language or the tenant default; pointing icons flip in right-to-left (kernel and DOM tests)

A stylesheet lint fails on a physical property (left, right, margin-left, padding-right and so on) outside an allow-list that names a reason, over web/src/styles and the generated token sheets (fixture with one violation)
The gallery matrix includes right-to-left (Arabic) and Japanese rows for every primitive and right-to-left for every pattern on desk (counted by the spec)
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457, revised after review round 1), "International and accessible by rule" and "The catalogue" (localisable from the first version).
