acceptance_criteria: web/test/golden holds page model, serialised DOM and pinned screenshot of every example for the current and previous rendering major; the previous major DOM and pixels are gated

The gate classifies as major a golden diff that adds, removes or renames a class outside the state-class allow-list, changes structure, or changes pixels of an existing example under exact comparison on the pinned image; otherwise minor and listed (fixtures)
A security fix may move goldens only with a Security-Fix: trailer naming a recorded task, applied to both majors, leaving goldens identical on both (fixture)

Every composition records the catalogue hash and contract version; /design/preview?contract=<major> draws the tenant real compositions through the production renderer path as a member, as anonymous and as each group (Playwright)

An end-of-support date and a grace period are set per major; owners get at least two warnings at separate builder sessions with a record of opening; owners who opened none are mailed; after the date the tenant is moved by one recorded definition step that re-checks compositions (reporting orphans) and re-runs the theme step; the owner can reverse it until the grace period ends; a tenant two majors behind is moved through each migration in turn (tests)

tests/corpus/ui holds showcase, synthetic and adversarial compositions; interpreter, formatter and derivation changes are gated on the page-model diff; anonymised exports enter only after an exporter and the owner privacy review
Manifest, shell and parts name the contract version; a mismatch is never drawn and shows the reload notice (kernel test)

On a floor notice the page purges interface parts of the old class at once, before the new manifest, and draws loading; any role change is treated as narrowing (simulator test with a failing part fetch)
A swap with no floor change is drawn only when every needed part and matching view replies are held; past the contact bound it shows an error state (simulator test)

The first shell of this programme handles 426 with Strata-Reload: 1 and a bootstrapped minimum version; the server refuses a minimum above the oldest shell version recorded as handling 426; index.html is no-store; a recorded fixture of that first shell reloads on a minimum bump (tests)
A tenant rendering major is tenant configuration (ui.renderingMajor) changed only by a recorded definition step, and the manifest names it (test)
Products target the lower supported major and are checked at install and upgrade against both supported majors catalogues; an entry only one major has is refused (test)

During a grace period three majors ship and the grace major goldens (DOM and pixels) are gated and receive every security fix; the end-of-grace move of a tenant that moved back is warned like the first move; a two-behind move runs at most two migrations (tests)
Tool-bump stacks keep every example within a per-example pixel bound and fall under the Baselines-Approved cap (fixture)
A Security-Fix: trailer names a Workgraph task the gate checks is tagged security and accepted (fixture)

Manifests, parts and the shell name the highest catalogue minor they use (largest since); a part needing a higher minor than the shell is never drawn and the platform bar shows the reload notice (kernel test)
A tenant move to a new major orphans base widgets that fail under it, shown to the owner in the preview before the date; the major release report lists every product whose base fails under it (tests)

Manifest entries name the highest catalogue minor per screen; a screen needing a higher minor than the shell is not drawn, the service worker installs the new shell, and the reload notice appears only once it is installed, activating when no queue drain runs (Playwright)

After a shell rollback, only stored parts the server no longer lists for the class are purged, an older stored part is kept and drawn until a drawable replacement is held, each part is purged at most once per manifest (no purge loop), and offline the older stored part is drawn (tests)

A reversal to the grace major restores the recorded before-state (major, orphaned entries), re-checks installed products base screens under that major with orphaning and a report, keeps theme tokens edited since the move and returns only untouched tokens to the previous derived set (contrast-checked), and keeps overlay edits only where they pass; a migration between majors transforms only the major setting, the theme derived set and the orphan record (tests)
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457, revised after review round 1), "Versioning: schemas and the rendering contract" and "Version skew". A rendering contract version per catalogue major, golden page models and DOM per example, the UI corpus replay, contract versions in manifest, shell and parts, reload on mismatch, the atomic manifest swap, minimum client version for reads.
tasks.title: Strata design system 19: rendering contract versions, golden outputs, corpus replay and version skew

acceptance_criteria: The composite body language is typed in the specification with open enums for node kinds and when operators (first version: primitive, layout, slot, heading with relative level, when with present, empty, equals, each at most one per path, actions); slot references are paths of at most three segments; reserved minor extensions: comparisons and not, image and icon nodes, a plural text node by Intl.PluralRules

The kernel refuses a composite that references itself, expands past 200 nodes, uses a gesture host or a landmark, has an unnamed interactive primitive (ui.a11y.unnamed-control), an image with no alt or decorative flag, or skipped heading levels (a refused fixture per code)

Composites in composite-typed host props are drawn once per item; the host injects the gesture handle as the first focusable of each item; Enter or F2 moves into the composite, Tab cycles inside, Escape returns; gesture keys belong to the handle (Playwright)
Composite templates are saved layouts with region constraints; the depth limit counts the expanded tree (tests)
Blocks ship a pricing table (its period toggle a screen filter), a hero, a media gallery and an FAQ with gallery examples
Renderer registry entries are data; a module whose hash does not match is not registered; capabilities is documentation until a verified-module manifest (stated in the code)

Gaps move through open, triaged, accepted or declined, resolved (resolvedBy) or duplicate (duplicateOf); a declined gap tells builders that its placeholders must be removed or replaced before publishing (tests)
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457, revised after review round 1), "Extending the catalogue". Product composites (typed slots, a body of primitives and layout containers) drawn by one generic renderer; composite templates; platform blocks; a renderer registry table for platform-reviewed extensions; POST /api/ui/gaps.
tasks.title: Strata design system 20: composite patterns and templates as data, platform blocks, renderer registry, catalogue gaps

acceptance_criteria: grouped bindings accept a closed field of at most 20 values, or a reference field whose lanes the product declares as a section read under the viewer policies (lanes paged); cards whose lane the viewer may not read go to a catch-all lane; a reference group without a lanes section is refused with ui.binding.open-group (tests)
series are computed by the kernel aggregate engine on the server, at most 500 points and 8 series, bucketed in the realm time zone with a declared bucket size and week start (tests)

positioned bindings require a window and return at most 2000 records plus the count in the window (test with 50000 records drawing at most 2000 nodes); plane images come from a file field or a tenant file, never a URL
chart is SVG via createElementNS, aria-hidden, with a data table from the same buckets as its accessible representation (Playwright with axe)
Screen filters are kernel state in the address and re-read sections taking a parameter of that name (kernel test)

The form-builder shape is typed: sections (drawable as wizard steps), closed input types including reference bound to a section, required, choices, closed validations, conditional visibility; answers are typed per input type as value variants, never a string list; reserved minor extensions not equals, or and repeating groups; calculation and branching are out of scope (kernel test, Playwright)

Record-defined form answers are written by a platform write-answers step as records of platform answer types per input type (answer_text, answer_number as int with the field scale, answer_date as time, answer_bool, answer_choice, answer_choices), one answer_ref_<object> type per object type the product declares forms may reference, with on-delete set-null, and one file answer type whose per-question limits are checked by the step; each type exists in four variants from two independent question flags, personal (subject the respondent, kind free-text, the product declared answer retention) and restricted (read rule has_role of the product fixed form-reviewer role); decimal, money, civil date and duration inputs wait for WG-5494 (kernel tests)
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457, revised after review round 1), "Structured bindings". grouped, series, positioned and record-form bindings with shapes served by the gateway; board, chart (SVG via DOM APIs with a data-table alternative), time-grid, plane, stream, dynamic-form and filter-bar patterns; screen filters as kernel state in the address.
tasks.title: Strata design system 21: structured bindings, charts, boards, time grids, planes, record-defined forms, shared filters

acceptance_criteria: Each gesture entry states a pure pending-write projection with examples, checked per example (kernel test)

move takes row.id, target.group and target.rank in one operation; ranks are fractional strings of at most 32 characters, ties ordered by rank then id; when no rank fits, the lane page is rebalanced in one operation before the gesture (tests including a collision)
inline-edit uses the input named per field type and refuses list, file and rich-text with ui.gesture.inline-unsupported (tests)
Each gesture works by keyboard alone and by single pointer without dragging (Playwright)

Wizard state lives in the kernel and in the encrypted drafts store under D-FE-13 rules when drafts are kept, in memory only for anonymous visitors, until submission, discard or the idle session lifetime, at most 64 KB, with only wizard and step in the address; step outputs prefill later steps (tests)
A reschedule gesture for time-grid is reserved in the catalogue as a minor extension with its keyboard path
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457, revised after review round 1), "Interaction". reorder, move, inline-edit and select-many gestures bound to operations with typed arguments, each with keyboard and single-pointer non-drag paths; wizard step state in the kernel; optimistic state only as kernel pending writes.
tasks.title: Strata design system 22: gestures, wizards and pending state

acceptance_criteria: specc emits with every bundle a provenance table mapping each entity id to the JSON Pointer that declared it, kept out of the installed schema (specc test)

Kernel schema refusals carry a catalogue code and the entity ids involved; the gateway maps them to pointers and lists every other entity involved in related, with pointers or, for another product or an overlay, their ids (tests per code family)

Every code states clears, the closed set of edits that remove it, where an entry may be the expand-optional, migrate, rebind, contract sequence; every refusal code has a negative fixture on which one clears entry (all upgrades of a sequence) makes it pass, including a cycle of three object types, a removal blocked by another product and a last-stage cap overflow; a fixture where a removal orphans an overlay entry is not refused and lists the entry in orphans (specc and kernel tests)
bundle_error replies with {code, severity, message, path, related, entity, catalogue, clears} for every product route refusal (tests)

The reference agent driver stops after a stated number of refused draft writes or upgrades and when the same code at the same path returns after its clears edit, except inside an expand, migrate, contract sequence (driver test with a restructure that is not counted as a failure)
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457, revised after review round 1), "Diagnostics and convergence". specc provenance table (entity id to JSON Pointer), kernel refusals with codes mapped to pointers by the gateway, the catalogue codes section with clears per code, negative fixtures, and the reference driver loop budget.
tasks.title: Strata design system 23: provenance and structured diagnostics with a convergence contract

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/ui/screens returns to a builder every live screen and, read from the draft store, every draft screen of a product, with widget, container and region ids; a non-builder is refused (gateway test)

GET /api/ui/bindings?screen= returns each view section with its shape and fingerprint, each form and action, and the patterns that accept each binding, for live screens and for draft screens through the preview projection (gateway test)
A holder of ui-build can read the tenant schema policies and operation invokers (test)

A tool runs the kernel and views headlessly (D-FE-10) against the gateway with an agent credential and returns the page model of a screen as a role set or anonymous, and a screenshot from the pinned environment (tool test)
The routes are documented in docs/protocol.md and in the catalogue served to agents
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457, revised after review round 1), "The agent build loop" (Read) and review finding D9. GET /api/ui/screens and /api/ui/bindings for builders, served shapes and fingerprints, schema read of policies and invokers for ui-build holders, and a page-model and screenshot tool built on the headless runner of D-FE-10.
tasks.title: Strata design system 24: the agent surface: screens, bindings, shapes, policy read, page-model and screenshot tool

acceptance_criteria: A scenario catalogue covers at least: long-running branching processes (parallel branches and joins, timers, escalations, compensation, versioning of in-flight instances, human tasks), organisation and access (legal entities, delegation, separation of duties, break-glass, impersonation, offboarding, reorganisations), data, time and compliance (currencies, fiscal calendars, time zones and DST, backdating and corrections, retention and legal holds, audit, e-signature, residency, bulk import), integrations and failure (external systems, partial failure, exception queues, reconciliation, outages, manual override), and industry stress tests
Every scenario has a verdict (supported, partial, missing) against the platform with file or spec references, and the unusual cases are concrete, not generic
Gaps are ranked by how many scenarios they block, and the top gaps are filed as Workgraph tasks with testable acceptance criteria, no time estimates
Findings that affect the design system are sent into its review loop (WG-5457)
tasks.description: Owner request 2026-11-22: think through everything an effectively arbitrary enterprise client might need, including long complex workflows with many steps and branches and unusual situations, and check Strata (backend kernel, automations, approvals, ledger, retention and subject rights, migrations, frontend engine docs/frontend.md, design system docs/design-system.md on design/design-system) against it. Five parallel analyses by area, synthesized into one catalogue with a supported / partial / missing verdict per scenario, code references, and gap tasks.
tasks.title: Enterprise scenario sweep: what an arbitrary enterprise client needs (long branching workflows, organisation and access, data/time/compliance, integrations and failure, industry stress tests), gap-analysed against Strata

acceptance_criteria: A test restores a tenant snapshot taken with a queued send-mail job and a queued call-webhook delivery, starts the worker, and observes no mail sent and no HTTP request made
Restored jobs are held as exception records the owner can release or drop, each listed by list-automation-exceptions
The outbox publisher after restore republishes no event whose sequence was already published before the restore point (test)
A requirement in the specification states the fence and names the test
tasks.description: Enterprise sweep (WG-5484) defect. rec-job is in the backup image and restore_snapshot is storage-only; D-6206/TEN-1212..1214 re-end sessions, grants and secrets but nothing fences restored jobs, so queued mail and call-webhook deliveries would send again. Forks already start with outbound off (TEN-1262/1263). Related: WG-5404 (restore runbook), WG-5420.
tasks.title: Restore must not re-fire outbound work: quiesce restored mail, webhook and outbox jobs

acceptance_criteria: A SCIM PATCH active:false on the only active owner is refused with a stated error and changes nothing (test)
A SCIM DELETE of the last owner is refused before any effect: sessions, disabled flag and group documents are unchanged afterwards (test compares state before and after)
Disabling an owner when another active owner exists still succeeds (test)
tasks.description: Enterprise sweep (WG-5484) defect. service/scim.rs::set_active sets the disabled flag without the owner-count check (ADM-1081 is enforced only in transition.rs::require_an_owner_remains), and SCIM delete disables, ends sessions and edits groups before failing at take_role, leaving a half-applied state.
tasks.title: SCIM must not disable or delete the last owner

acceptance_criteria: A test runs an automation whose loop visits the same fan-out step twice and observes the leaf step applied once per member per visit
Keys for in-flight runs created before the change still resolve (test with a stored run from the old key form, or a stated migration)
tasks.description: Enterprise sweep (WG-5484), by inspection: worker/fan_out.rs:43 member_key uses the step-key/v1 form without the run's step sequence, so a fan-out step revisited in a loop may reuse the first visit's recorded member results. Related: WG-5427.
tasks.title: Fan-out member key must include the step-visit sequence

acceptance_criteria: A test issues two decisions for the same pending approval from two store handles interleaved between read and write; exactly one succeeds and the other returns conflict
The run advances exactly once (one next-step job exists)
tasks.description: Enterprise sweep (WG-5484): approve_step_at reads the run, then automation_write; whether the store makes the write conditional on the read state was not verified. WFL-2683 requires a single decision. Related: WG-5427.
tasks.title: Concurrent approval decisions: the decision write must be conditional on the state read

acceptance_criteria: A step option makes the run wait for the delivery outcome; a test with a receiver returning 500 on every attempt shows the step failing and the run's compensations running in reverse order
A test with a receiver returning 200 shows the step completing with the response status bound as a step output
Runs pinned to definitions without the option behave as before (test)
tasks.description: Enterprise sweep (WG-5484): AutomationStepResult::CallWebhook completes with status 0 when queued; a later delivery failure dead-letters the delivery job, not the step, so saga compensation never fires for an external failure. Add a distinct awaiting variant (do not mutate the existing one; runs pin definitions).
tasks.title: A call-webhook step's real delivery outcome must reach the run

acceptance_criteria: A members-manage holder can suspend a local person: their sessions and tokens end and sign-in is refused (test); reactivation restores sign-in
Suspending the last active owner is refused (test)
An administrator can end another person's sessions through a contract; open sockets close (test)
Each action is in the change audit with the acting administrator
tasks.description: Enterprise sweep (WG-5484): local accounts cannot be deactivated (PrincipalState exists in model/records but is not enforced); revoke_own_session (auth.rs:517) only ends the caller's own sessions; a person with every role revoked keeps public and can still sign in.
tasks.title: Local account suspension and administrator session revocation

acceptance_criteria: A test sends the same Strata-Event-Id twice with different bodies; the second is refused with idempotency-mismatch and starts no run
Identical repeats are still answered as repeats (test)
tasks.description: Enterprise sweep (WG-5484): outbound/inbound.rs dedupes by event id for 7 days without comparing the body; operations raise idempotency-mismatch for the same case.
tasks.title: Inbound webhook: a repeated event id with a different body is reported, not absorbed

acceptance_criteria: Record-created/updated/deleted triggers bind the record id as param.record; a test automation updates the triggering record from it
Automations declare typed run variables, type-checked by automation_params; a test sets a variable in one step and branches on it three steps later

A step expression can read fields of a record by id under the automation principal's policies, with the read declared as a Need; a test shows a field the principal cannot read is refused, not returned
Operation steps gain a guard (condition per step) and a lookup by unique field; a test operation refuses when the guard is false and changes nothing
The Lean model and differential suite cover every added expression form (verification test passes with a mutant caught)
tasks.description: Enterprise gap G1 (WG-5484), the most-blocking gap: blocks all ten industry sketches. Record triggers bind only seq/at/hop/transition (kernel/src/triggers.rs:177); step expressions evaluate with no record (worker/steps.rs act); run parameters are a fixed vocabulary (kernel/src/definitions.rs:191); operation steps are create/update/delete/post only. Reads of balances, segments and settings are WG-5417 (D-6543..6545) and are a dependency, not duplicated here. Mind D2 coverage (declared Needs) and the Lean mirror of Expr.
tasks.title: Automations and operations can read and act on case data

acceptance_criteria: A product can declare a dependency on another product and reference its object types; install refuses when the dependency is absent or at an incompatible version (tests)
Removing a product that another installed product references is refused with the dependants named (test)
A tenant-wide role can hold permissions across products; the showcase admin needs one role instead of five (fixture)
Upgrading the referenced product with a breaking change to a referenced field is refused by the evolution check (test)
tasks.description: Enterprise gap G2 (WG-5484): layer.cross-product-reference in crates/spec-compiler/src/layers.rs refuses a product referencing another product's entities; roles are product-namespaced (showcase gaps 1 and 2; enterprise corpus README items 1-8). Every industry sketch has one person or record across modules.
tasks.title: Cross-product references and tenant-wide roles

acceptance_criteria: Decisions recorded in the specification for: a decimal type (precision, scale, rounding modes), money as amount plus currency, date and duration types, zone-aware conversion, and division (replacing or amending D-6540, D-6541)
Rust kernel, JS frontend kernel and Lean model agree on every operation over a generated differential corpus including rounding edge cases (half-even, negative values, scale overflow)
A ledger unit can carry a scale; a test posts 0.01 increments 10,000 times and the balance is exactly 100.00
Adding a month to 31 January and crossing a DST change produce the documented results (tests)
tasks.description: Enterprise gap G3 (WG-5484): field types are str/int/bool/time/ref/list/file/language; no decimal, money, date, duration or zone; no division (D-6540) or calendar arithmetic (D-6541, rationale lapsed); ledger ints to 2^53-1. Blocks eight industries. The value algebra is closed across Rust, JS and Lean: decide the design first, as decisions, before code.
tasks.title: Exact numbers and civil time in the value algebra

acceptance_criteria: A run can split into parallel branches and join with all, any or N-of-M; a test with three branches completing in random order joins exactly once
Multi-instance over a list field or record query runs one branch per item, including waits and approvals in each (test with N decided at runtime)
A wait-for-signal step resumes when a correlated record event or inbound webhook arrives; a late signal for a closed run is recorded, not lost (tests)
A call step starts a child run, waits, and binds its outputs; cancelling the parent cancels the child (test)
approve-workflow-step identifies the branch, and existing single-cursor runs keep working (test)
tasks.description: Enterprise gap G4 (WG-5484): runs have one cursor (RunRecord.step, job key step:{run}:{seq}); fan-out iterates segment members with one leaf that cannot wait; no wait-for-signal; inbound webhooks start new runs only; no call step; declared-event has no emit path (D-8201). Closing it changes the run record, job keys and approve-workflow-step (which takes only a run id): do it before many runs exist.
tasks.title: Process structure: parallel branches, joins, quorum, multi-instance, reactive waits, call activity

acceptance_criteria: A task step takes an assignee expression (person, role, or a person field on the case) and a decision form whose outcome and comment are bound as run variables (test)
Pool tasks can be claimed, released and reassigned by an authorised person; a reassign is audited (tests)
A pending-for-me contract lists only tasks the caller may decide, without automations-read (test with two people)
A tenant screen can decide a task through a declared UI action; the BFF route is no longer the only path (end-to-end test)
Separation of duties can name an earlier step's decider, not only the starter (test)
tasks.description: Enterprise gap G5 (WG-5484): approvals name a static role; no assignee expression, claim, reassign or per-person pending view (list-automation-runs needs automations-read); the tenant UI can only invoke operations and operations cannot approve. Separation of duties only against the run starter.
tasks.title: Human-task primitive and task inbox

acceptance_criteria: Contracts cancel, suspend and resume one run; a suspended run's timers and approval deadlines do not fire, and resume reschedules them by the paused duration (tests)
An owner can skip a failed step or jump to a named step, audited (test)
A decision can be revoked within a declared window, running the compensations of steps completed since (test)
An owner can extend a pending deadline (test)
A business rollback step runs compensations without a failure (test)
tasks.description: Enterprise gap G6 (WG-5484): no cancel-run (cancel-job leaves the run waiting); suspending an automation cancels in-flight runs (steps.rs:628); no suspended RunState; compensation fires only on step failure; decisions are final and deadlines immutable.
tasks.title: Run lifecycle control: cancel, suspend, resume, repair, reopen, revoke

acceptance_criteria: A tenant calendar object holds zone, working days and holidays, with versions
A wait or deadline can be 'N working days' on a calendar; a test across a weekend and a holiday lands on the documented instant
Adding a holiday after a deadline was set recomputes live deadlines that fall on it (test)
A clock can be paused while a case waits on the customer and resumed, the deadline moving by the paused working time (test)

tasks.description: Proposed by docs/design-system.md (WG-5457, round 4, finding F4): FieldDef has no derived or computed member (crates/model-core/src/types.rs:4895-4912; default is evaluated once at creation), so a condition over computed state (overdue, over budget) must be a stored field kept up to date by operations or automations. acceptance_criteria: An upgrade can declare a migration (copy or convert a field to another, by a conversion from the open platform vocabulary); the platform runs it as a job in batches of erasure::BATCH records, each batch one commit (backend test with more than MAX_SCAN_RECORDS records)
Migration writes emit an event of kind migration that no trigger or automation matches; a fixture with a trigger on the type shows it does not fire (test)
Progress (the last record id done) lives in the job state, not in any record; a restarted job resumes from it (test that kills the job between batches)

The rebind upgrade is one commit that replaces the product operations, forms and actions with versions writing only the new field, relaxes the old field to optional, freezes it, runs the last pass, and rebinds the screens and owner-approved overlay entries; the planner refuses it with migration.writers-remain while any product writer still writes the field being frozen (kernel tests)
plan_migration no longer loads all records of a type in one transition: existing migrations use the job, or are refused past MAX_SCAN_RECORDS with a code naming the job (test)

The expand step adds the new field optional (a required field on a type with records is refused, ExistingData::Reject); the contract step may tighten it to required once the job reports zero left (tests)

The migration event reaches segments (re-evaluated), notices and stamps, the search index, aggregate copies and erasure like any write, and only triggers and automations do not match it; one test per consumer

The job is durable and resumes after a crash; values that do not convert are reported with a clears naming an approved data-fix step; the owner sees its status; while it runs an upgrade altering the migrating fields is refused with migration.in-progress (or queued), while changes to read rules, policies and invokers of the type go through (tests including a security-fix upgrade)

The expand upgrade carries, atomically, the operation changes that make the product writers write both fields; catch-up passes run until the rebind commit; the owner may choose the fallback sequence (a separate approved freeze, then the last pass, then rebind) after repeated migration.not-ready, accepting the stale-read window (tests)
Conversions come from an open, platform-released vocabulary (first identity, int to text, text to int, time to date, choice rename); an unknown conversion is refused (test)
The new field read rule and personal declaration must be the same as or stricter than the source field; a migration to a less protected field is refused (test)

field.frozen refuses a write that changes the frozen field value, from record intents, other products, automations, imports and write-answers, and accepts a write carrying the value unchanged; subject erasure and retention, which write outside record-change validation, still erase and expire it; a test per path

Undo after the rebind commit declares a reverse migration with the inverse conversion, whose own rebind commit lifts the freeze on the old field and freezes the new one under the same at-most-one-batch rule; an undo whose conversion has no inverse is refused with migration.not-invertible naming it (tests); before the rebind commit undo cancels the job

The rebind commit requires a complete report from the job (every record of the type at a version written at or before the report sequence S copied, no unconverted value left), else migration.not-ready with the job status; its last pass covers only records changed after S, through a new Need variant record-events-after {object, after} added to the need type in the specification and served by Store::events_after, refused with migration.not-ready if more than erasure::BATCH distinct records changed, else setting each loaded record new field to the conversion of the old where they differ (kernel tests: refused with the bulk copy incomplete; refused with an unconverted record; a record written after the report still copied, or the commit refused)

The expand upgrade raises the old field to the new field read rule and personal declaration until contract, shown in the permission delta; subject erasure after the rebind commit removes both copies (test)

The reverse migration commit changes the writers to the old field only, relaxes and freezes the new field, runs the last pass by the same Need and bound, and binds back; its destination must be same as or stricter than its source, else migration.not-invertible (tests including a personal field)

A fixture renames a required field through expand, bulk copy, the rebind commit and contract with a live product writer making changes in every phase, and checks every write succeeds and no value is lost

The rebind commit rewrites every reader of the old field, or the planner refuses with migration.dependents-remain naming them: the dependency graph dependents (queries, policies, workflows, triggers, automations, views, constraints, unique constraints, field rules, references, object settings), two new DependentId kinds built from closed forms, Operation (conditions, subject, step expressions) and Template (typed value nodes in mail and notice templates), and a planner scan of segment predicates in the segment store; fixtures where a policy condition, a query filter, an operation condition, a segment predicate and a template each name the old field

The rebind commit is one ChangeSchema within the 200-change cap; when its writers, dependents, screens and overlay rebinds exceed it, it is refused with migration.rebind-too-large naming the count and the restructure falls back to the separate freeze sequence, each step within the cap (test)

Segment predicates naming the old field are rewritten to the new field after the job has a complete report and before the rebind commit; migration.dependents-remain refuses the rebind commit while a segment rewrite has not finished; a fixture kills the process between the segment rewrite and the commit and checks segment membership stays consistent, with SegmentEntered and SegmentExited triggers acting on correct membership

The Operation and Template DependentId kinds change impact analysis for every schema change: assess_changes classifies a field change read by an operation (conditions, subject, steps) or a template value node by those dependents (D-8210), rewrite_schema rewrites them when a field is renamed or moved, and MIG-592 is amended in the specification to name operations and templates among affected dependents (kernel tests for a rename and a breaking change of a field an operation and a template read)
tasks.description: docs/design-system.md (WG-5457), Restructures: expand, migrate, contract as ordinary approved upgrades. Migration becomes a platform job instead of plan_migration's single transition (crates/kernel/src/transition.rs:1948), which loads every record of a type at once (no bound against MAX_SCAN_RECORDS) and whose writes reach triggers. The job copies or converts values in batches of erasure::BATCH records (crates/backend/src/erasure.rs, crates/kernel/src/erasure.rs), emits a migration event kind no trigger matches, and keeps its progress in the job state, not in records.
tasks.title: Strata: data migrations as platform jobs in bounded batches, invisible to triggers

tasks.description: Owner direction 2026-11-26, after WG-5673 found that erasing a person can leave records that break constraints, unique values or workflow states (and proposed holding such records unerased): none of hold / break / refuse is acceptable; fix the architecture. Treat personal data erasure as a first-class kernel primitive, distinct from account deactivation and ordinary record deletion. Design explicit erasure semantics into the metamodel: field classification, relationships, constraints, uniqueness, workflow states, historical records, derived data, retention policies and automation execution. Erasure must not silently violate kernel invariants, nor may ordinary tenant-defined constraints arbitrarily prevent erasure: introduce legitimate erased lifecycle states (e.g. an erased value/state every constraint, unique rule and workflow must accept) and validate schema and workflow compatibility with erasure at publication time (schema change refused if a definition could block erasure). Preserve necessary non-identifying business facts and transactional integrity while removing identifying information; account for indirect identification, historical versions, indexes (search, unique), caches (browser copies, copy store), event streams (outbox, events, segment logs) and backups. Any retained personal information needs an explicit, justified, auditable retention policy. Investigate the existing architecture and specification holistically first (docs/storage.md, docs/frontend.md erasure epochs, specifications on subject rights, erasure.rs, retention.rs, subject_export.rs, sealed fields, key destruction D-7720..7728), then update the specification, kernel, Lean model and end-to-end verification together. WG-5673's branch fv/wg5673 holds the Lean erasure/expiry model and a kernel change (commit 38735ec4, hold-on-break) that must not land as is.
tasks.title: Personal data erasure as a first-class kernel primitive (redesign before WG-5673 lands)
